354:       .map(a => ({
355:         id: a.id,
356:         object: 'model' as const,
357:         created: 0,
358:         owned_by: 'freellmapi',
359:         name: a.displayName,
360:         context_window: autoContextWindow,
361:         context_length: autoContextWindow,
362:         available: true,
363:         unavailable_reason: null,
364:       }))
365:     : [];
366: 
367:   res.json({
368:     object: 'list',
369:     data: [
370:       {
371:         id: AUTO_MODEL_ID,
372:         object: 'model',
373:         created: 0,
374:         owned_by: 'freellmapi',
375:         name: 'Auto (router picks the best available model)',
376:         context_window: autoContextWindow,
377:         // `context_length` is OpenRouter's field name and the one most
378:         // OpenAI-compatible clients read; emit both so whichever a client
379:         // looks for is populated. Additive — clients ignore unknown fields.
380:         context_length: autoContextWindow,

432: // Echo-tolerant tool calls: agents replay OUR responses back as history, and
433: // not all of them preserve the strict OpenAI shape. `type` may be dropped
434: // (re-added on forward), Gemini-lineage agents (Qwen Code, AionUI) often
435: // send `arguments` as a parsed object instead of a JSON string, and `id` may
436: // be missing or empty (ids aren't a Gemini concept) — all get normalized
437: // below rather than 400-ing the whole session. Missing ids are synthesized
438: // and paired with their tool-result messages by order. (#200)
439: const toolCallSchema = z.object({
440:   id: z.string().optional(),
441:   type: z.literal('function').optional(),
442:   function: z.object({
443:     name: z.string().min(1),
444:     arguments: z.union([z.string(), z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())]),

447: });

450:   typeof args === 'string' ? args : JSON.stringify(args);

452: // OpenAI multimodal envelope. Clients like opencode / continue.dev send
453: // content as an array of typed blocks even when only text is present, and
454: // Gemini-lineage agents send part-style blocks like `{ "text": "..." }` with
455: // no `type` at all. Accept any object (or bare string) as a block; flatten to
456: // string for providers that don't support arrays (Cohere, Cloudflare).
457: // Non-text blocks pass z validation but get dropped by contentToString —
458: // vision/audio still isn't supported. (#200)
459: const contentBlockSchema = z.union([z.string(), z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())]);
460: const contentSchema = z.union([z.string(), z.array(contentBlockSchema)]);

462: const systemMessageSchema = z.object({
463:   role: z.literal('system'),
464:   content: contentSchema,
465:   name: z.string().optional(),
466: });

469: // and forward as "system" — none of the routed providers know the developer
470: // role. (#200)

483: // Assistant turns may carry empty/null content and no tool_calls — OpenAI
484: // accepts these in conversation history (a turn that produced no visible text,
485: // a placeholder, a tool turn whose content was emptied), and clients replay
486: // them verbatim. We accept them too and coerce empty/null content to "" before

594: // Pull the incremental text out of a streaming chunk for token counting.
595: // Must tolerate chunks that carry no `choices` array at all: some providers
596: // (e.g. Groq) emit usage/keepalive frames shaped like `{usage:{...}}` with no
597: // `choices`. Indexing `chunk.choices[0]` on those throws "Cannot read
598: // properties of undefined (reading '0')", which — once the SSE stream has
599: // started — aborts the response mid-flight with no chance to fall back.
600: export function streamChunkText(chunk: any): string {
601:   return chunk?.choices?.[0]?.delta?.content ?? '';

604: // Pull the incremental reasoning text out of a streaming chunk. Reasoning
605: // models stream thinking via `reasoning_content` (Z.ai, DeepSeek-style — the
606: // <think> extractor in base.ts normalizes inline tags into the same field) or
607: // `reasoning` (Ollama-style) before the first visible answer token; both
608: // spellings must count for ttfb and output-token estimates. Same shape
609: // tolerance as streamChunkText. (#764)
610: export function streamReasoningText(chunk: any): string {
611:   const delta = chunk?.choices?.[0]?.delta;
612:   const r = delta?.reasoning_content ?? delta?.reasoning;
613:   return typeof r === 'string' ? r : '';

712:   if (!requireInferenceAuth(req, res)) return;

715:     res.status(400).json({
716:       error: {
717:         message: 'Invalid request: `prompt` is required and video options must use supported values',
718:         type: 'invalid_request_error',
719:       },

725:   // fail over to a second one, both charged to the operator, for a response
726:   // nobody is waiting for. 'close' also fires on normal completion, which
727:   // writableEnded distinguishes.
728:   const clientAbort = new AbortController();
729:   res.on('close', () => {
730:     if (!res.writableEnded) clientAbort.abort();

733:     const result = await runVideoGeneration(parsed.data.model, {
734:       prompt: parsed.data.prompt,

738:       seed: parsed.data.seed,
739:       audio: parsed.data.audio,

742:     res.setHeader('Cache-Control', 'no-store');
743:     res.setHeader('X-Provider', safeHeaderValue(result.platform));
744:     res.setHeader('X-Model', safeHeaderValue(result.modelId));
745:     res.send(result.video);

747:     // Nothing to report to a socket that is already gone.
748:     if (clientAbort.signal.aborted || res.writableEnded) return;
749:     const status = err instanceof MediaError ? err.status : 502;
750:     const httpStatus = status >= 400 && status < 600 ? status : 502;

255: // ── Dynamic priority: track 429s per model and demote accordingly ──
256: // Key: model_db_id → { count, lastHit, penalty }
257: const rateLimitPenalties = new Map<number, { count: number; lastHit: number; penalty: number }>();
258: 
259: // Penalty decays over time so models recover
260: const PENALTY_PER_429 = 3;        // each 429 adds this many priority positions
261: const PENALTY_PER_FAIL = 1;       // each non-limit upstream failure (5xx/timeout/empty stream)
262: const MAX_PENALTY = 10;            // cap so a model doesn't sink forever
263: const DECAY_INTERVAL_MS = 2 * 60 * 1000; // penalty decays every 2 minutes
264: const DECAY_AMOUNT = 1;            // remove this much penalty per decay interval
265: 
266: /**
267:  * Record an upstream failure for a model — increases its penalty so it sinks in
268:  * priority. Default weight is the LIGHT one for ordinary upstream failures
269:  * (5xx/timeout/empty stream, +1); callers that know they saw a hard limit
270:  * signal (429/402) pass the heavier weight — a quota limit is the stronger,
271:  * longer-lived health cue.
272:  */
273: export function recordModelFailure(modelDbId: number, weight = PENALTY_PER_FAIL) {
274:   const existing = rateLimitPenalties.get(modelDbId);
275:   const now = Date.now();
276:   if (existing) {
277:     const decaySteps = Math.floor((now - existing.lastHit) / DECAY_INTERVAL_MS);
278:     existing.penalty = Math.max(0, existing.penalty - decaySteps * DECAY_AMOUNT);
279:     existing.count++;
280:     existing.lastHit = now;
281:     existing.penalty = Math.min(existing.penalty + weight, MAX_PENALTY);
282:   } else {
283:     rateLimitPenalties.set(modelDbId, { count: 1, lastHit: now, penalty: weight });
284:   }
285: }
286: 
287: /**
288:  * Record a 429 for a model — heavier penalty (priority demotion) than ordinary
289:  * failures, since a rate-limit signal is the strongest short-term health cue.
290:  */
291: export function recordRateLimitHit(modelDbId: number) {
292:   recordModelFailure(modelDbId, PENALTY_PER_429);
293: }
294: 
295: /**
296:  * Record a success for a model — reduces its penalty so it rises back up.
297:  */
298: export function recordSuccess(modelDbId: number) {
299:   const existing = rateLimitPenalties.get(modelDbId);
300:   if (existing) {
301:     existing.penalty = Math.max(0, existing.penalty - 1);
302:     if (existing.penalty === 0) {
303:       rateLimitPenalties.delete(modelDbId);
304:     }
305:   }
306: }
307: 
308: /**
309:  * Get the current penalty for a model (with time-based decay).
310:  * Pure read — does not mutate the entry; decay is applied lazily only when
311:  * recording a new hit (recordRateLimitHit) so the clock isn't reset on every
312:  * routing call.
313:  */
314: function getPenalty(modelDbId: number): number {
315:   const entry = rateLimitPenalties.get(modelDbId);
316:   if (!entry) return 0;
317: 
318:   const elapsed = Date.now() - entry.lastHit;
319:   const decaySteps = Math.floor(elapsed / DECAY_INTERVAL_MS);
320:   const decayed = Math.max(0, entry.penalty - decaySteps * DECAY_AMOUNT);
321:   if (decayed === 0) {
322:     rateLimitPenalties.delete(modelDbId);
323:     return 0;
324:   }
325:   return decayed;
326: }
327: 
328: /**
329:  * Get current penalties for all models (for the API/dashboard).
330:  */
331: export function getAllPenalties(): Array<{ modelDbId: number; count: number; penalty: number }> {
332:   const result: Array<{ modelDbId: number; count: number; penalty: number }> = [];
333:   for (const [modelDbId, entry] of rateLimitPenalties) {
334:     const penalty = getPenalty(modelDbId);
335:     if (penalty > 0) {
336:       result.push({ modelDbId, count: entry.count, penalty });
337:     }
338:   }
339:   return result.sort((a, b) => b.penalty - a.penalty);
340: }

342: // ── Routing strategy (persisted) ────────────────────────────────────────────
343: const STRATEGY_KEY = 'routing_strategy';
344: const CUSTOM_WEIGHTS_KEY = 'routing_custom_weights';
345: const EXPLORE_KEY = 'routing_explore_enabled';
346: const PEAK_ADJUST_KEY = 'routing_peak_hours_adjust';
347: const PEAK_START_KEY = 'routing_peak_start_hour';
348: const PEAK_END_KEY = 'routing_peak_end_hour';
349: const PEAK_TZ_KEY = 'routing_peak_timezone';
350: const COMMUNITY_PRIOR_KEY = 'routing_community_prior';
351: const COMMUNITY_PRIOR_ENABLED_KEY = 'routing_community_prior_enabled';
352: // Headroom guardrail thresholds (#899): the remaining-budget fraction at which
353: // demotion begins and the score floor at 0 remaining. Stored as decimals
354: // (0.2 = 20%). Absent/invalid values fall back to the scoring.ts constants so
355: // existing installs are untouched.
356: export const HEADROOM_RAMP_START_KEY = 'routing_headroom_ramp_start';
357: export const HEADROOM_FLOOR_KEY = 'routing_headroom_floor';
358: 
359: export function getHeadroomThresholds(): { rampStart: number | undefined; floor: number | undefined } {
360:   const read = (key: string): number | undefined => {
361:     const raw = getSetting(key);
362:     if (raw === undefined || raw.trim() === '') return undefined;
363:     const n = Number(raw);
364:     return Number.isFinite(n) && n >= 0 && n <= 1 ? n : undefined;
365:   };
366:   return { rampStart: read(HEADROOM_RAMP_START_KEY), floor: read(HEADROOM_FLOOR_KEY) };
367: }
368: 
369: // null clears a threshold back to the default; undefined leaves it untouched.
370: export function setHeadroomThresholds(rampStart?: number | null, floor?: number | null): void {
371:   const db = getDb();
372:   const apply = (key: string, value: number | null | undefined): void => {
373:     if (value === undefined) return;
374:     if (value === null) {
375:       db.prepare('DELETE FROM settings WHERE key = ?').run(key); // back to default
376:       return;
377:     }
378:     if (!Number.isFinite(value) || value < 0 || value > 1) {
379:       throw new Error(`Invalid value ${value} for ${key} (must be 0..1)`);
380:     }
381:     setSetting(key, String(value));
382:   };
383:   apply(HEADROOM_RAMP_START_KEY, rampStart);
384:   apply(HEADROOM_FLOOR_KEY, floor);
385: }

387: /** Chance per request that an unmeasured model gets tried first when the
388:  *  exploration toggle is on. The bandit's Thompson sampling already explores
389:  *  automatically; this guarantees a floor so models with no reliability/speed
390:  *  data still get sampled instead of being starved by prior-heavy rivals. */
391: export const EXPLORE_CHANCE = 0.1;
392: /** A model counts as "has data" once its decay-weighted success+failure
393:  *  pseudo-count reaches this many samples. */
394: export const EXPLORE_MIN_SAMPLES = 5;
395: const VALID_STRATEGIES: RoutingStrategy[] = ['priority', 'balanced', 'smartest', 'fastest', 'reliable', 'custom'];
396: 
397: export function getRoutingStrategy(): RoutingStrategy {
398:   const raw = getSetting(STRATEGY_KEY);
399:   return (raw && VALID_STRATEGIES.includes(raw as RoutingStrategy))
400:     ? (raw as RoutingStrategy)
401:     : DEFAULT_STRATEGY;
402: }

404: export function setRoutingStrategy(strategy: RoutingStrategy): void {
405:   if (!VALID_STRATEGIES.includes(strategy)) {
406:     throw new Error(`Unknown routing strategy: ${strategy}`);
407:   }
408:   setSetting(STRATEGY_KEY, strategy);
409: }

412: // Off by default: existing routing behavior unchanged. When on, routeRequest
413: // gives unmeasured models a guaranteed chance to be tried (EXPLORE_CHANCE) so
414: // they acquire reliability/speed samples instead of losing every bandit draw.
415: export function getExploreEnabled(): boolean {
416:   return getSetting(EXPLORE_KEY) === '1';

423: // ── Peak-hours adjustment (persisted, off by default) ──────────────────────
424: // Opt-in time-of-day reweighting (#760). Everything about it is operator-set:
425: // whether it runs at all, the window, and the timezone the window is read in.
426: // With the flag off, weightsFor returns the presets byte-for-byte, so an
427: // install that never touches this setting routes exactly as it did before.
428: export function getPeakHoursConfig(): PeakHoursConfig {
429:   const startRaw = Number.parseInt(getSetting(PEAK_START_KEY) ?? '', 10);
430:   const endRaw = Number.parseInt(getSetting(PEAK_END_KEY) ?? '', 10);
431:   const tzRaw = getSetting(PEAK_TZ_KEY);
432:   return {
433:     enabled: getSetting(PEAK_ADJUST_KEY) === '1',
434:     startHour: isValidPeakHour(startRaw) ? startRaw : DEFAULT_PEAK_HOURS.startHour,
435:     endHour: isValidPeakHour(endRaw) ? endRaw : DEFAULT_PEAK_HOURS.endHour,
436:     timezone: isValidTimezone(tzRaw) ? tzRaw : DEFAULT_PEAK_HOURS.timezone,
437:   };
438: }

440: /** Persist any subset of the peak-hours settings. Throws on an out-of-range
441:  *  hour or an unknown IANA timezone so a bad PUT is rejected at the API rather
442:  *  than silently stored and then ignored on read. */
443: export function setPeakHoursConfig(patch: Partial<PeakHoursConfig>): void {
444:   if (patch.startHour !== undefined && !isValidPeakHour(patch.startHour)) {
445:     throw new Error('peakStartHour must be an integer between 0 and 23');
446:   }
447:   if (patch.endHour !== undefined && !isValidPeakHour(patch.endHour)) {
448:     throw new Error('peakEndHour must be an integer between 0 and 23');
449:   }
450:   if (patch.timezone !== undefined && !isValidTimezone(patch.timezone)) {
451:     throw new Error('peakTimezone must be a valid IANA timezone name');
452:   }
453:   if (patch.enabled !== undefined) setSetting(PEAK_ADJUST_KEY, patch.enabled ? '1' : '0');
454:   if (patch.startHour !== undefined) setSetting(PEAK_START_KEY, String(patch.startHour));
455:   if (patch.endHour !== undefined) setSetting(PEAK_END_KEY, String(patch.endHour));
456:   if (patch.timezone !== undefined) setSetting(PEAK_TZ_KEY, patch.timezone);
457: }

461: // picked. Independent of the routing strategy on purpose (#919): the strategy
462: // enum drives the MODEL bandit, so putting a key policy in it would make
463: // choosing a key policy also throw away the model ranking.

465: //                       round-robin otherwise.
466: //   'least-remaining' — additionally rank by observed remaining quota, roomiest
467: //                       key first, so the key closest to its cap is held back
468: //                       instead of being the next one to 429.
469: const KEY_SELECTION_KEY = 'key_selection_strategy';
470: const VALID_KEY_SELECTIONS: KeySelectionStrategy[] = ['auto', 'least-remaining'];
471: export const DEFAULT_KEY_SELECTION: KeySelectionStrategy = 'auto';

487: // ── Custom weights (persisted) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
488: // User-tuned weight vector for the 'custom' strategy. Stored normalized (sums
489: // to 1) so the dashboard percentages read cleanly; combineScore would tolerate
490: // any non-negative vector regardless. Falls back to the balanced preset until
491: // the user has saved their own.
492: export function getCustomWeights(): RoutingWeights {
493:   const raw = getSetting(CUSTOM_WEIGHTS_KEY);
494:   if (raw) {
495:     try {
496:       const w = JSON.parse(raw) as RoutingWeights;
497:       if (
498:         [w.reliability, w.speed, w.intelligence].every(v => Number.isFinite(v) && v >= 0) &&
499:         w.reliability + w.speed + w.intelligence > 0
500:       ) {
501:         return { reliability: w.reliability, speed: w.speed, intelligence: w.intelligence };
502:       }
503:     } catch { /* corrupt setting → fall through to default */ }
504:   }
505:   return { ...BANDIT_PRESETS.balanced };
506: }
507: 
508: export function setCustomWeights(weights: RoutingWeights): void {
509:   const { reliability, speed, intelligence } = weights;
510:   if (![reliability, speed, intelligence].every(v => Number.isFinite(v) && v >= 0)) {
511:     throw new Error('Custom weights must be non-negative numbers');
512:   }
513:   const sum = reliability + speed + intelligence;
514:   if (sum <= 0) {
515:     throw new Error('Custom weights must not all be zero');
516:   }
517:   setSetting(CUSTOM_WEIGHTS_KEY, JSON.stringify({
518:     reliability: reliability / sum,
519:     speed: speed / sum,
520:     intelligence: intelligence / sum,
521:   }));
522: }

524: // ── Community reliability prior (persisted) ────────────────────────────────
525: // Aggregated, de-poisoned counts from other self-hosted instances, folded into
526: // the Beta posterior as a starting balance so a brand-new model isn't blind
527: // (#685 follow-up). Keyed "platform:model_id" (endpoint-scoped keys use the
528: // same modelStatsKey form). Local samples dilute it automatically.
529: //
530: // Opt-in: priors only reach the posterior when routing_community_prior_enabled
531: // is on (default off). Server-side only for now — there is deliberately no
532: // ingestion path yet, so the flag pins the opt-in semantics before one lands.
533: type CommunityPriorMap = Record<string, { successes: number; failures: number }>;
534: 
535: /** Ceiling on a single prior's effective sample size. Local counts are
536:  *  decay-weighted (2-day half-life — a busy install still only carries on the
537:  *  order of a hundred effective samples), so an unbounded, undecayed community
538:  *  count would drown local evidence forever and collapse the Thompson-sampling
539:  *  variance to zero. Capping at ~50 pseudo-observations keeps a prior worth
540:  *  roughly half the local evidence at most: enough to seed a brand-new model,
541:  *  cheap for real local traffic to override. */
542: export const COMMUNITY_PRIOR_MAX_SAMPLES = 50;
543: 
544: /** Validate a raw prior map and cap each entry's effective sample size.
545:  *  Shared by the read path and the write path so a value is bounded no matter
546:  *  how it entered (fresh set, legacy stored blob, hand-edited settings row).
547:  *  Invalid entries (negative, all-zero, no ':') are dropped; oversized ones
548:  *  are rescaled preserving the success/failure ratio (980/20 → 49/1). */
549: function sanitizeCommunityPriors(priors: unknown): CommunityPriorMap {
550:   const clean: CommunityPriorMap = {};
551:   if (!priors || typeof priors !== 'object') return clean;
552:   for (const [key, v] of Object.entries(priors as Record<string, { successes: number; failures: number }>)) {
553:     if (
554:       key.includes(':') &&
555:       v && typeof v === 'object' &&
556:       Number.isFinite(v.successes) && v.successes >= 0 &&
557:       Number.isFinite(v.failures) && v.failures >= 0 &&
558:       v.successes + v.failures > 0
559:     ) {
560:       const total = v.successes + v.failures;
561:       const scale = total > COMMUNITY_PRIOR_MAX_SAMPLES ? COMMUNITY_PRIOR_MAX_SAMPLES / total : 1;
562:       const entry = { successes: Math.round(v.successes * scale), failures: Math.round(v.failures * scale) };
563:       if (entry.successes + entry.failures > 0) clean[key] = entry;
564:     }
565:   }
566:   return clean;
567: }
568: 
569: // Parsed-prior cache, same 60s shape as the stats cache: routing reads the map
570: // once per chain entry (and once per key in orderKeysByScore), so hitting
571: // sqlite + JSON.parse on every lookup is pure waste. Invalidated by the two
572: // setters and by refreshStatsCache, so tests and future ingestion see writes
573: // immediately.
574: let communityPriorCache: { map: CommunityPriorMap; enabled: boolean } | null = null;
575: let communityPriorCacheTime = 0;
576: 
577: function communityPriorState(): { map: CommunityPriorMap; enabled: boolean } {
578:   const now = Date.now();
579:   if (communityPriorCache && now - communityPriorCacheTime < CACHE_TTL_MS) return communityPriorCache;
580:   let map: CommunityPriorMap = {};
581:   const raw = getSetting(COMMUNITY_PRIOR_KEY);
582:   if (raw) {
583:     try {
584:       map = sanitizeCommunityPriors(JSON.parse(raw));
585:     } catch { /* corrupt setting → no priors */ }
586:   }
587:   communityPriorCache = { map, enabled: getSetting(COMMUNITY_PRIOR_ENABLED_KEY) === '1' };
588:   communityPriorCacheTime = now;
589:   return communityPriorCache;
590: }
591: 
592: function invalidateCommunityPriorCache(): void {
593:   communityPriorCache = null;
594: }
595: 
596: /** Whether stored community priors are folded into the posterior. Default off. */
597: export function getCommunityPriorEnabled(): boolean {
598:   return communityPriorState().enabled;
599: }
600: 
601: export function setCommunityPriorEnabled(enabled: boolean): void {
602:   setSetting(COMMUNITY_PRIOR_ENABLED_KEY, enabled ? '1' : '0');
603:   invalidateCommunityPriorCache();
604: }
605: 
606: /** Community prior for one model, or undefined when none is stored.
607:  *  Raw read — ignores the enabled flag; routing goes through
608:  *  activeCommunityPrior, which honors it. */
609: export function getCommunityPrior(platform: string, modelId: string, endpointScope?: string):
610:   { successes: number; failures: number } | undefined {
611:   return communityPriorState().map[modelStatsKey(platform, modelId, endpointScope)];
612: }
613: 
614: /** Gated read for routing: undefined unless the opt-in flag is on. */
615: function activeCommunityPrior(platform: string, modelId: string, endpointScope?: string):
616:   { successes: number; failures: number } | undefined {
617:   const state = communityPriorState();
618:   return state.enabled ? state.map[modelStatsKey(platform, modelId, endpointScope)] : undefined;
619: }
620: 
621: /** Replace the whole community-prior map (e.g. after an aggregation fetch).
622:  *  Invalid entries are dropped and oversized ones capped, never stored raw. */
623: export function setCommunityPriors(priors: CommunityPriorMap): number {
624:   const clean = sanitizeCommunityPriors(priors);
625:   setSetting(COMMUNITY_PRIOR_KEY, JSON.stringify(clean));
626:   invalidateCommunityPriorCache();
627:   return Object.keys(clean).length;
628: }
629: 
630: /** Active weights plus whether the peak-hours adjustment (#760) changed them.
631:  *  With the setting off (the default) `weights` is the preset itself and
632:  *  `adjusted` is false, so nothing about routing moves with the clock.
633:  *  priority/custom are the operator's explicit choice and are never rewritten. */
634: function weightsWithPeak(strategy: RoutingStrategy): { weights: RoutingWeights | null; adjusted: boolean } {
635:   if (strategy === 'priority') return { weights: null, adjusted: false };
636:   if (strategy === 'custom') return { weights: getCustomWeights(), adjusted: false };
637:   return peakAdjustedWeights(BANDIT_PRESETS[strategy], strategy, getPeakHoursConfig());
638: }
639: 
640: function weightsFor(strategy: RoutingStrategy): RoutingWeights | null {
641:   return weightsWithPeak(strategy).weights;
642: }
643: 
644: /** The weight vector routing will use right now for the active strategy, and
645:  *  whether the peak-hours adjustment moved it. Cheap (settings reads only) —
646:  *  for the PUT /routing echo, which must not pay for a full score sweep. */
647: export function getActiveRoutingWeights(): { weights: RoutingWeights | null; adjusted: boolean } {
648:   return weightsWithPeak(getRoutingStrategy());
649: }

651: // ── Analytics stats cache (decay-weighted) ──────────────────────────────────
652: // Instead of the fork's flat 7-day window (where a model that degrades today
653: // keeps a stale week-long average), each request is weighted by an exponential
654: // decay so recent behavior dominates while older data still stabilizes the
655: // estimate. We aggregate by (model, integer day age) in SQL — at most ~7 rows
656: // per model — then apply the per-bucket decay weight in JS.
657: const WINDOW_MS = 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;
658: const HALF_LIFE_DAYS = 2; // a 2-day-old request counts half as much as a fresh one
659: const CACHE_TTL_MS = 60 * 1000;
660: 
661: interface ModelStats {
662:   successes: number;   // decay-weighted pseudo-count
663:   failures: number;    // decay-weighted pseudo-count
664:   // Output tokens from successes over the time spent on successes AND timeouts
665:   // (#619 — see the accumulator below); 0 = no data.
666:   tokPerSec: number;
667:   avgTtfbMs: number | null; // null = no first-byte timing yet
668:   monthlyUsedTokens: number; // calendar-month usage, for the headroom guardrail
669:   // Decay-weighted requests that actually SAY something about speed: successes
670:   // plus timeouts. A model can have hundreds of 401s and still no speed signal,
671:   // so this — not successes + failures — is what gates the observed speed_rank
672:   // writeback.
673:   speedSamples: number;
674: }
675: 
676: // Per-key slice of the same window (#580): reliability/speed observed through
677: // ONE credential of a model. With unified groups, a model's traffic can span
678: // several keys whose real quality diverges (expired, quota-drained, region-
679: // blocked keys fail while siblings are fine) — the rolled-up model bucket
680: // can't see that, so key selection needs its own buckets.
681: interface KeyStats {
682:   successes: number;   // decay-weighted pseudo-count
683:   failures: number;    // decay-weighted pseudo-count
684:   tokPerSec: number;   // from successful requests only (0 = no data)
685:   avgTtfbMs: number | null;
686: }
687: 
688: // Keyed by modelStatsKey(): "platform:model_id" for catalog models, and
689: // "custom:model_id@base_url" for a relay model that carries an endpoint scope
690: // (#651). A single-endpoint install produces the same keys it always did.
691: let statsCache: Map<string, ModelStats> | null = null;
692: let keyStatsCache: Map<string, KeyStats> | null = null; // "platform:model_id:key_id"
693: let statsCacheTime = 0;
694: 
695: function decayWeight(ageDays: number): number {
696:   return Math.pow(0.5, Math.max(0, ageDays) / HALF_LIFE_DAYS);
697: }
698: 
699: // SQL predicate for "this row is a timed-out request" (#619). A timeout is an
700: // error row whose text carries one of the shared timeout markers
701: // (lib/error-classify.ts), which is also what the failover attempt trail
702: // classifies on. 'canceled' rows (#752 — client hung up) never reach this
703: // predicate: the stats query below filters them out entirely, because a
704: // vanished client says nothing about the model's reliability or speed. The
705: // markers are hard-coded lowercase identifiers from our own source, never
706: // user input, so interpolating them into the LIKE list is safe.
707: const IS_TIMEOUT_SQL = `(status != 'success' AND (${
708:   TIMEOUT_ERROR_MARKERS.map(m => `LOWER(COALESCE(error, '')) LIKE '%${m}%'`).join(' OR ')
709: }))`;
710: 
711: /** api_keys.id → endpoint scope, for every custom credential on record (#651). */
712: function customEndpointScopes(db: Db): Map<number, string> {
713:   const rows = db.prepare("SELECT id, base_url FROM api_keys WHERE platform = 'custom'")
714:     .all() as { id: number; base_url: string | null }[];
715:   return new Map(rows.map(r => [r.id, endpointScopeForBaseUrl(r.base_url)]));
716: }
717: 
718: export function refreshStatsCache(db: Db, force = false): void {
719:   if (!force && statsCache && Date.now() - statsCacheTime < CACHE_TTL_MS) return;
720: 
721:   // Re-read the community priors alongside the stats they season, so a forced
722:   // refresh (tests, admin actions) never routes on a stale prior snapshot.
723:   invalidateCommunityPriorCache();
724: 
725:   const since = new Date(Date.now() - WINDOW_MS).toISOString();
726:   // Grouped by (model, key, day age): still a handful of rows per model — key
727:   // count × ≤7 day buckets — so the finer grain keeps the same one-query,
728:   // 60s-cached shape. Aggregated two ways below: rolled up per model (ordering)
729:   // and per key (in-model key selection, #580).
730:   const buckets = db.prepare(`
731:     SELECT platform, model_id, key_id,
732:       CAST((julianday('now') - julianday(created_at)) AS INTEGER) AS age_days,
733:       COUNT(*) AS total,
734:       SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'success' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS successes,
735:       SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'success' THEN output_tokens ELSE 0 END) AS succ_out,
736:       SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'success' THEN latency_ms ELSE 0 END) AS succ_lat,

1180:            m.supports_tools, m.context_window, m.key_id, m.endpoint_scope
1181:     FROM models m
1182:     LEFT JOIN fallback_config fc ON fc.model_db_id = m.id
1183:     ${profileId != null ? 'LEFT JOIN profile_models pm ON pm.profile_id = ? AND pm.model_db_id = m.id' : ''}
1184:     WHERE m.enabled = 1 AND ${chainEnabled}
1185:   `).all(...(profileId != null ? [profileId] : [])) as ChainRow[];
1186: 
1187:   const strategyMap: Record<string, RoutingStrategy> = {
1188:     'smart': 'smartest',
1189:     'fast': 'fastest',
1190:     'cheap': 'balanced',
1191:     'reliable': 'reliable',
1192:     'balanced': 'balanced'
1193:   };
1194:   const strat = strategyMap[globalAxis] || 'balanced';
1195:   
1196:   return orderChain(allEnabled, strat);
1197: }

1199: /**
1200:  * The active chain, or a client-facing refusal when it has nothing enabled.
1201:  *
1202:  * Mirrors what `auto:<name>` already does for a named chain: say the chain is
1203:  * empty rather than routing the request over models the operator never put in
1204:  * it. Only when a profile is active — a legacy install with none keeps the
1205:  * ordinary "all models exhausted" exhaustion path.
1206:  */
1207: function activeChainOrThrow(db: Db): ChainRow[] {
1208:   const chain = getActiveChain(db);
1209:   if (chain.some(entry => entry.enabled)) return chain;
1210: 
1211:   const profileId = getActiveProfileId(db);
1212:   if (profileId == null) return chain;
1213: 
1214:   const profile = db.prepare('SELECT name FROM profiles WHERE id = ?').get(profileId) as { name: string } | undefined;
1215:   const err = new Error(
1216:     `The active fallback chain${profile ? ` '${profile.name}'` : ''} has no enabled models. `
1217:     + 'Enable models for it on the Models page, switch the active chain, or name another one with "auto:<chain>".',
1218:   ) as any;
1219:   err.status = 400;
1220:   throw err;
1221: }

1223: export function resolveRoutingChain(modelString: string | undefined): ResolvedChain {
1224:   const db = getDb();
1225: 
1226:   if (!modelString || modelString.toLowerCase() === 'auto') {
1227:     return { chain: activeChainOrThrow(db), strategyKey: 'auto' };
1228:   }
1229: 
1230:   const lower = modelString.toLowerCase();
1231:   if (!lower.startsWith('auto:')) {
1232:     return { chain: activeChainOrThrow(db), strategyKey: 'auto' };
1233:   }
1234: 
1235:   const suffix = lower.slice('auto:'.length).trim();
1236:   if (!suffix) {
1237:     return { chain: activeChainOrThrow(db), strategyKey: 'auto' };
1238:   }
1239: 
1240:   const globalAxis = GLOBAL_SORT_ALIASES[suffix];
1241:   if (globalAxis) {
1242:     const chain = getChainByGlobalSort(db, globalAxis);
1243:     if (chain.length === 0) {
1244:       const err = new Error(`No enabled models available for global sort '${suffix}'`) as any;
1245:       err.status = 400;
1246:       throw err;
1247:     }
1248:     return { chain, strategyKey: `auto:${globalAxis}` };
1249:   }
1250: 
1251:   const chain = getChainByProfileName(db, suffix);
1252:   if (!chain) {
1253:     const err = new Error(`Profile '${suffix}' not found. Use 'auto' for the default profile, or call /v1/models for available options.`) as any;
1254:     err.status = 400;
1255:     throw err;
1256:   }
1257: 
1258:   const enabledModels = chain.filter(e => e.enabled);
1259:   if (enabledModels.length === 0) {
1260:     const err = new Error(`Profile '${suffix}' has no enabled models. Add models to this profile in the dashboard.`) as any;
1261:     err.status = 400;
1262:     throw err;
1263:   }
1264: 
1265:   return { chain, strategyKey: `auto:${suffix}` };
1266: }

1268: // Weights for the in-model key score (#580). Reliability dominates: the point
1269: // of per-key stats is catching a credential that FAILS (expired, drained,
1270: // region-blocked); speed differences between keys of the same platform+model
1271: // are second-order (account-tier throttling) but still worth a nudge.
1272: const KEY_SCORE_WEIGHTS = { reliability: 0.75, speed: 0.25 };
1273: 
1274: /**
1275:  * Order a model's candidate keys by a Thompson-sampled per-key score, mirroring
1276:  * orderChain's bandit: reliability is a fresh draw from each key's Beta
1277:  * posterior (so exploration is automatic and proportional to uncertainty — a
1278:  * key with no data samples from the uniform prior and still gets traffic),
1279:  * speed is deterministic. Returns null when NO key has recorded data, telling
1280:  * the caller to keep the legacy round-robin rotation (no signal → no ranking).
1281:  */
1282: function orderKeysByScore(entry: ChainRow, keys: KeyRow[]): KeyRow[] | null {
1283:   if (keys.length < 2 || !keyStatsCache) return null;
1284:   const prefix = `${modelStatsKey(entry.platform, entry.model_id, entry.endpoint_scope)}:`;
1285:   if (!keys.some(k => keyStatsCache!.has(prefix + k.id))) return null;
1286: 
1287:   // The prior is per-model, not per-key: look it up once outside the loop.
1288:   const community = activeCommunityPrior(entry.platform, entry.model_id, entry.endpoint_scope);
1289:   return keys
1290:     .map(k => {
1291:       const stats = keyStatsCache!.get(prefix + k.id);
1292:       const { alpha, beta } = reliabilityPosterior(stats?.successes ?? 0, stats?.failures ?? 0, community);
1293:       const rel = sampleBeta(alpha, beta);
1294:       const spd = speedScore(stats?.tokPerSec ?? 0, stats?.avgTtfbMs ?? null);
1295:       return { k, s: KEY_SCORE_WEIGHTS.reliability * rel + KEY_SCORE_WEIGHTS.speed * spd };
1296:     })
1297:     .sort((a, b) => b.s - a.s || a.k.id - b.k.id)
1298:     .map(x => x.k);
1299: }

1301: /** Headroom assumed for a key the quota tracker has never seen. Neutral on
1302:  *  purpose: an unobserved budget is no reason to prefer a key (it could be
1303:  *  drained) and no reason to avoid one (it could be untouched), so it sorts
1304:  *  between an exhausted key and a fresh one and otherwise keeps its incoming
1305:  *  round-robin position. */
1306: const UNKNOWN_QUOTA_HEADROOM = 0.5;
1307: 
1308: /**
1309:  * Whether remaining-quota weighting is meaningful for this chain entry: the
1310:  * operator asked for it AND the platform meters its keys separately.
1311:  *
1312:  * An account-scoped pool ('<platform>::account') is ONE budget every key of the
1313:  * account draws down, so "which key has more left" has no answer — every key
1314:  * reports the same number, and reordering on it would only churn the rotation
1315:  * for nothing (#919).
1316:  */
1317: function quotaWeightingApplies(entry: ChainRow): boolean {
1318:   if (getKeySelectionStrategy() !== 'least-remaining') return false;
1319:   return !inferQuotaPoolKey(entry.platform as Platform, entry.model_id).endsWith('::account');
1320: }
1321: 
1322: /**
1323:  * Re-order an already-ordered candidate list by observed remaining quota,
1324:  * roomiest first (#919 — the issue asks for higher-remaining-first, so the key
1325:  * nearest its cap is tried last, not first).
1326:  *
1327:  * Deliberately a SORT over the caller's list rather than a second walk: the
1328:  * incoming order is the round-robin rotation (or the per-key bandit ranking),
1329:  * and Array#sort is stable, so keys with equal headroom — including the common
1330:  * case of no observations at all — keep exactly the order they would have had.
1331:  * Every gate, the custom-endpoint filter and the skip tally stay in the one
1332:  * walk that follows.
1333:  */
1334: function orderKeysByRemainingQuota(entry: ChainRow, ordered: KeyRow[]): KeyRow[] {
1335:   const headroom = getKeyQuotaHeadroom(entry.platform as Platform);
1336:   if (headroom.size === 0) return ordered;
1337:   // Hoisted out of the comparator: sort calls it O(n log n) times, and the
1338:   // lookup below must not re-derive anything per comparison.
1339:   const room = new Map(ordered.map(k => [k.id, headroom.get(k.id) ?? UNKNOWN_QUOTA_HEADROOM]));
1340:   return [...ordered].sort((a, b) => room.get(b.id)! - room.get(a.id)!);
1341: }

1343: /**
1344:  * Pick a usable key for ONE model and build its RouteResult, or return null if
1345:  * the model has no key that can serve the request right now (all cooled down,
1346:  * over quota, undecryptable, or no provider). Factored out of routeRequest so
1347:  * the fusion panel can HARD-PIN a model: walk that model's keys without ever
1348:  * falling through to a different model (issue #326 — soft preference collapses
1349:  * panel diversity under rate limits). Keys are tried in per-key bandit-score
1350:  * order when any of them has recorded data (#580), else round-robin.
1351:  * Request-level filters (vision/tools/context window) stay in the caller; this
1352:  * only does key selection + accounting pre-checks.
1353:  */
1354: function selectKeyForModel(entry: ChainRow, estimatedTokens: number, skipKeys?: Set<string>, diag?: string[]): RouteResult | null {
1355:   const db = getDb();
1356:   const label = `${entry.platform}/${entry.model_id}`;
1357: 
1358:   if (!hasProvider(entry.platform as Platform)) {
1359:     diag?.push(`${label}: no provider registered`);
1360:     return null;
1361:   }
1362:   const provider = getProvider(entry.platform as Platform)!;
1363: 
1364:   const allKeys = db.prepare(
1365:     "SELECT * FROM api_keys WHERE platform = ? AND enabled = 1 AND status IN ('healthy', 'unknown')"
1366:   ).all(entry.platform) as KeyRow[];
1367:   if (allKeys.length === 0) {
1368:     diag?.push(`${label}: no enabled+healthy key for platform`);
1369:     return null;
1370:   }
1371: 
1372:   // Scoped keys (#657) are dropped before the walk: a key whose model scope
1373:   // excludes this model is not a candidate at all — it neither takes a
1374:   // round-robin slot nor burns an attempt on a guaranteed 403. Parsed once per
1375:   // key row.
1376:   const keys = allKeys.filter(k => scopeAllows(parseModelScope(k.model_scope_json), entry.model_id));
1377:   if (keys.length === 0) {
1378:     diag?.push(`${label}: no usable key — ${allKeys.length} key(s) scoped to other models`);
1379:     return null;
1380:   }
1381: 
1382:   // Tally the gate that rejected each key, so the exhaustion diagnostic can say
1383:   // *why* a model with keys still couldn't serve (all on cooldown vs over quota).
1384:   const skipTally: Record<string, number> = {};
1385:   const note = (reason: string) => { skipTally[reason] = (skipTally[reason] ?? 0) + 1; };
1386: 
1387:   const limits = {
1388:     rpm: entry.rpm_limit,
1389:     rpd: entry.rpd_limit,
1390:     tpm: entry.tpm_limit,
1391:     tpd: entry.tpd_limit,
1392:   };
1393: 
1394:   // Score-ordered walk over this model's keys (#580): when any key has recorded
1395:   // reliability/speed data, try them best-sampled-score first so a chronically
1396:   // failing key stops soaking up every Nth request. The stats cache is the same
1397:   // 60s-TTL aggregate the model-level bandit uses (refresh is a no-op when
1398:   // fresh, and cheap when not). With no data at all, keep the legacy rotation.
1399:   refreshStatsCache(db);
1400:   // Scoped so two relays offering the same model id don't share one rotation
1401:   // cursor over the platform's key list (#651).
1402:   const rrKey = modelStatsKey(entry.platform, entry.model_id, entry.endpoint_scope);
1403:   let idx = roundRobinIndex.get(rrKey) ?? 0;
1404:   let ranked = orderKeysByScore(entry, keys);
1405: 
1406:   // Remaining-quota weighting (#919) layers on top: it re-sorts whatever order
1407:   // we were going to walk anyway — the bandit ranking when there is per-key
1408:   // data, otherwise the round-robin rotation starting at the live cursor — so
1409:   // ties fall back to that order instead of to rowid.
1410:   if (keys.length > 1 && quotaWeightingApplies(entry)) {
1411:     const base = ranked ?? Array.from({ length: keys.length }, (_, i) => keys[(idx + i) % keys.length]);
1412:     ranked = orderKeysByRemainingQuota(entry, base);
1413:   }
1414: 
1415:   // A custom model belongs to exactly one endpoint (#212), but an endpoint can
1416:   // hold several credentials — so the pool is every key on the same base_url,
1417:   // rotated like any other platform's keys (#619). Legacy rows (key_id NULL)
1418:   // keep the old any-key match.
1419:   const endpointKeyIds = entry.platform === 'custom' && entry.key_id != null
1420:     ? customEndpointKeyIds(db, entry.key_id)
1421:     : null;
1422: 
1423:   for (let attempt = 0; attempt < keys.length; attempt++) {
1424:     const key = ranked ? ranked[attempt] : keys[idx % keys.length];
1425:     idx++;
1426: 
1427:     if (endpointKeyIds && !endpointKeyIds.has(key.id)) { note('custom-key-mismatch'); continue; }
1428: 
1429:     const skipId = `${entry.platform}:${entry.model_id}:${key.id}`;
1430:     if (skipKeys?.has(skipId)) { note('already-failed-this-request'); continue; }
1431: 
1432:     if (isOnCooldown(entry.platform, entry.model_id, key.id)) { note('cooldown'); continue; }
1433:     if (!canUseProvider(entry.platform, key.id)) { note('provider-daily-cap'); continue; }
1434:     // Account-wide per-minute budget, checked before the per-model gates: a model
1435:     // with a NULL rpm_limit would otherwise sail past them and spend a budget its
1436:     // siblings share.
1437:     if (!canUseProviderMinute(entry.platform, key.id)) { note('provider-minute-cap'); continue; }
1438:     // Skip a key that already has its allowed requests in the air. Without this,
1439:     // parallel streams all pick the same key and 429 each other on providers that
1440:     // meter concurrency per credential.
1441:     if (!canUseKeyConcurrency(entry.platform, key.id)) { note('key-concurrency'); continue; }
1442:     if (!canMakeRequest(entry.platform, entry.model_id, key.id, limits)) { note('rpm/rpd-limit'); continue; }
1443:     if (!canUseTokens(entry.platform, entry.model_id, key.id, estimatedTokens, limits)) { note('tpm/tpd-limit'); continue; }
1444:     if (!canUseProviderTokens(entry.platform, key.id, entry.model_id, estimatedTokens)) { note('provider-daily-token-cap'); continue; }
1445: 
1446:     let decryptedKey: string;
1447:     try {
1448:       decryptedKey = decrypt(key.encrypted_key, key.iv, key.auth_tag);
1449:     } catch {
1450:       db.prepare("UPDATE api_keys SET status = 'error', last_checked_at = datetime('now') WHERE id = ?")
1451:         .run(key.id);
1452:       note('decrypt-error');
1453:       continue;
1454:     }
1455: 
1456:     const resolvedProvider = entry.platform === 'custom'
1457:       ? resolveProvider('custom', key.base_url)
1458:       : provider;
1459:     if (!resolvedProvider) { note('no-resolved-provider'); continue; }
1460: 
1461:     roundRobinIndex.set(rrKey, idx);
1462:     // Taken only once the key has cleared every gate and is definitely being
1463:     // returned, so a rejected candidate never consumes concurrency budget.
1464:     const leaseId = acquireLease(entry.platform, entry.model_id, key.id, estimatedTokens);
1465:     return {
1466:       provider: resolvedProvider,
1467:       modelId: entry.model_id,
1468:       modelDbId: entry.model_db_id,
1469:       apiKey: decryptedKey,
1470:       keyId: key.id,
1471:       keyLabel: key.label || null,
1472:       // Decrypted once here, at the point the row is already in hand (#590).
1473:       proxyUrl: decryptProxyUrl(key),
1474:       platform: entry.platform,
1475:       displayName: entry.display_name,
1476:       endpointScope: entry.endpoint_scope ?? '',
1477:       rpdLimit: limits.rpd,
1478:       tpdLimit: limits.tpd,
1479:       release: () => releaseLease(leaseId),
1480:     };
1481:   }
1482: 
1483:   // No usable key for this model. Advance the round-robin index anyway so we
1484:   // don't get stuck re-trying the same exhausted key first next time.
1485:   roundRobinIndex.set(rrKey, idx);
1486:   const summary = Object.entries(skipTally).map(([r, n]) => `${r}:${n}`).join(', ') || 'no usable key';
1487:   diag?.push(`${label}: ${keys.length} key(s) — ${summary}`);
1488:   return null;
1489: }

1491: /**
1492:  * Whether the model still has ANOTHER key that could serve it right now, given
1493:  * the key that just failed (excludingKeyId) and any keys already ruled out this
1494:  * request (skipKeys, in the "platform:modelId:keyId" form). Applies the same
1495:  * gates selectKeyForModel uses — enabled + healthy status, not on cooldown,
1496:  * under the provider daily cap, and under rpm/rpd/tpm/tpd — so the answer means
1497:  * "a real, dispatchable alternative exists".
1498:  *
1499:  * Used by the retry loops to decide whether a single key's 429 should demote the
1500:  * WHOLE model (the model-level 429 penalty). It should not: the per-key cooldown
1501:  * already isolates the failing key, so demoting the model while a sibling key can
1502:  * still serve it wrongly sinks a healthy model in the scorer (#454). We only
1503:  * record the model-level hit when this returns false — i.e. the 429 exhausted the
1504:  * model, not just one of its keys.
1505:  */
1506: export function hasOtherUsableKey(modelDbId: number, excludingKeyId: number, skipKeys?: Set<string>): boolean {
1507:   const db = getDb();
1508:   const m = db.prepare(`
1509:     SELECT platform, model_id, rpm_limit, rpd_limit, tpm_limit, tpd_limit, key_id
1510:       FROM models WHERE id = ?
1511:   `).get(modelDbId) as {
1512:     platform: string; model_id: string;
1513:     rpm_limit: number | null; rpd_limit: number | null;
1514:     tpm_limit: number | null; tpd_limit: number | null; key_id: number | null;
1515:   } | undefined;
1516:   if (!m) return false;
1517: 
1518:   const limits = { rpm: m.rpm_limit, rpd: m.rpd_limit, tpm: m.tpm_limit, tpd: m.tpd_limit };
1519:   const keys = db.prepare(
1520:     "SELECT id, model_scope_json FROM api_keys WHERE platform = ? AND enabled = 1 AND status IN ('healthy', 'unknown')"
1521:   ).all(m.platform) as { id: number; model_scope_json: string | null }[];
1522: 
1523:   // Keys of the model's own custom endpoint (#212, #619); a key belonging to a
1524:   // DIFFERENT endpoint cannot serve it, so it doesn't count as an alternative.
1525:   const endpointKeyIds = m.platform === 'custom' && m.key_id != null
1526:     ? customEndpointKeyIds(db, m.key_id)
1527:     : null;
1528: 
1529:   for (const k of keys) {
1530:     if (k.id === excludingKeyId) continue;
1531:     if (endpointKeyIds && !endpointKeyIds.has(k.id)) continue;
1532:     // A sibling scoped away from this model can never serve it (#657) — counting
1533:     // it would wrongly suppress the model-level penalty this gate exists for.
1534:     if (!scopeAllows(parseModelScope(k.model_scope_json), m.model_id)) continue;
1535:     if (skipKeys?.has(`${m.platform}:${m.model_id}:${k.id}`)) continue;
1536:     if (isOnCooldown(m.platform, m.model_id, k.id)) continue;
1537:     if (!canUseProvider(m.platform, k.id)) continue;
1538:     if (!canUseProviderMinute(m.platform, k.id)) continue;
1539:     if (!canMakeRequest(m.platform, m.model_id, k.id, limits)) continue;
1540:     // A per-minute token spike on the failed key doesn't mean a fresh key lacks
1541:     // headroom; a nominal 1-token probe only rules out a key already at its
1542:     // TPM/TPD ceiling.
1543:     if (!canUseTokens(m.platform, m.model_id, k.id, 1, limits)) continue;
1544:     if (!canUseProviderTokens(m.platform, k.id, m.model_id, 1)) continue;
1545:     return true;
1546:   }
1547:   return false;
1548: }

1550: /**
1551:  * Every key that can be ROUTED to this model: enabled + healthy/unknown, not
1552:  * scoped away from the model (#657), and — for a custom model — belonging to
1553:  * the model's own endpoint (#212, #619). Deliberately ignores the transient
1554:  * gates hasOtherUsableKey applies (cooldown, quotas): the caller here is the
1555:  * model-level bench, which needs the full key set to take a sick model out of
1556:  * rotation, not "who could serve the next request".
1557:  */
1558: export function routableKeyIdsForModel(modelDbId: number): number[] {
1559:   const db = getDb();
1560:   const m = db.prepare('SELECT platform, model_id, key_id FROM models WHERE id = ?')
1561:     .get(modelDbId) as { platform: string; model_id: string; key_id: number | null } | undefined;
1562:   if (!m) return [];
1563: 
1564:   const keys = db.prepare(
1565:     "SELECT id, model_scope_json FROM api_keys WHERE platform = ? AND enabled = 1 AND status IN ('healthy', 'unknown')"
1566:   ).all(m.platform) as { id: number; model_scope_json: string | null }[];
1567: 
1568:   const endpointKeyIds = m.platform === 'custom' && m.key_id != null
1569:     ? customEndpointKeyIds(db, m.key_id)
1570:     : null;
1571: 
1572:   return keys
1573:     .filter(k => !endpointKeyIds || endpointKeyIds.has(k.id))
1574:     .filter(k => scopeAllows(parseModelScope(k.model_scope_json), m.model_id))
1575:     .map(k => k.id);
1576: }

1578: /**
1579:  * Fetch a single enabled model's chain row by its db id.
1580:  */
1581: function getModelChainRow(db: Db, modelDbId: number): ChainRow | undefined {
1582:   return db.prepare(`
1583:     SELECT m.id as model_db_id, 0 as priority, 1 as enabled,

1588:     FROM models m
1589:     WHERE m.id = ? AND m.enabled = 1

1593: /**
1594:  * Safety margin applied when ranking a model against an estimated request size.
1595:  * The estimate is a chars/4 heuristic that under-counts dense payloads (JSON,
1596:  * code, CJK) by up to ~2x; without any accounting for that gap such requests
1597:  * were routed to models whose real tokenizer count exceeded the window and the
1598:  * provider rejected them with a 400 mid-chain (kilo: "maximum context length is
1599:  * 262144 tokens" on requests estimated <=256000).
1600:  *
1601:  * The margin is a SOFT preference, not a hard filter (#956 review): /v1/models
1602:  * advertises the RAW window, so clients legitimately pack requests right up to
1603:  * it. Excluding margin-violating models outright would turn an upstream 400
1604:  * that the retry loop already classifies and handles (`context_too_large`)
1605:  * into a regression: "all models exhausted" with zero attempts. Callers
1606:  * therefore try margin-fitting candidates first and only fall back to raw
1607:  * advertised-window fits (see fitsContextWindowStrict) when nothing else can
1608:  * serve the request.
1609:  */
1610: export const CONTEXT_WINDOW_SAFETY_FACTOR = 1.25;
1611: 
1612: // Platforms whose pre-dispatch trim guard already caps the dispatched input
1613: // below the live context ceiling (lib/content.ts truncateMessagesForGithub):
1614: // the guard — not the routing estimate — is what guarantees the fit there, so
1615: // applying the factor too would only make that guard unreachable. The margin
1616: // checks below treat these platforms as strict comparisons.
1617: const TRIM_GUARDED_PLATFORMS = new Set(['github']);
1618: 
1619: /** True when `estimatedTokens` fits the RAW advertised window (null window =
1620:  * unknown, never filtered — same convention as the auto-router). This is the
1621:  * comparison /v1/models publishes and the soft-preference fallback tier. */
1622: export function fitsContextWindowStrict(contextWindow: number | null | undefined, estimatedTokens: number): boolean {
1623:   return contextWindow == null || estimatedTokens <= contextWindow;
1624: }
1625: 
1626: /** True when `estimatedTokens` plausibly fits `contextWindow` WITH the safety
1627:  * margin. The chars/4 heuristic portion is scaled by the factor; an explicit
1628:  * output reserve derived from the client's max_tokens (`routingReserveTokens`)
1629:  * is already an exact count and is added UNSCALED (#956 review). Trim-guarded
1630:  * platforms compare strictly — their guard guarantees the fit. */
1631: export function fitsContextWindow(platform: string, contextWindow: number | null | undefined, estimatedTokens: number, exactOutputReserve = 0): boolean {
1632:   if (contextWindow == null) return true;
1633:   // Raw advertised comparison first — the margin can only shrink eligibility.
1634:   if (estimatedTokens > contextWindow) return false;
1635:   if (TRIM_GUARDED_PLATFORMS.has(platform)) return true;
1636:   const reserve = Math.max(0, exactOutputReserve);
1637:   const heuristic = Math.max(0, estimatedTokens - reserve);
1638:   return heuristic * CONTEXT_WINDOW_SAFETY_FACTOR + reserve <= contextWindow;
1639: }
1640: 
1641: /**
1642:  * Route to ONE specific model, hard-pinned. Rotates across that model's keys
1643:  * (cooldowns, quotas, decryption all honored) but NEVER substitutes a different
1644:  * model — returns null if the pinned model can't serve right now. This is what
1645:  * makes a fusion panel genuinely diverse: a rate-limited slot is dropped, not
1646:  * silently collapsed onto whatever else is available. `skipKeys` lets a slot
1647:  * exclude keys it already failed on this request.
1648:  */
1649: export function routePinnedModel(modelDbId: number, estimatedTokens = 1000, skipKeys?: Set<string>): RouteResult | null {
1650:   const db = getDb();
1651:   const entry = getModelChainRow(db, modelDbId);
1652:   if (!entry) return null;
1653:   // Strict comparison only (#956 review): a pinned slot has no substitute, so
1654:   // refusing on a margin violation would drop the slot outright where the
1655:   // pre-margin behavior was one dispatch attempt (a mid-chain context_too_large
1656:   // 400 is classified and retried downstream). Nothing is multiplied here —
1657:   // estimatedTokens already carries the exact capped output reserve (#470).
1658:   if (!fitsContextWindowStrict(entry.context_window, estimatedTokens)) return null;
1659:   if (entry.tpm_limit != null && estimatedTokens > entry.tpm_limit) return null;
1660:   return selectKeyForModel(entry, estimatedTokens, skipKeys);
1661: }

1663: /**
1664:  * Resolve a logical model group's member db ids to an ordered ChainRow[] for
1665:  * strict group-pin routing (the "unify" feature). Each catalog-enabled member
1666:  * is hydrated as a ChainRow carrying its active-profile/manual priority, then
1667:  * ordered by the active strategy via orderChain. Auto-chain enabled/disabled is
1668:  * intentionally ignored here because an explicit model request should still be
1669:  * able to use a direct model that the user removed from auto routing.
1670:  *
1671:  * Pass the result to routeRequest() as `prefetchedChain` and DO NOT pass a
1672:  * `preferredModelDbId` that isn't already one of these rows — otherwise the
1673:  * preferred-model injection in routeRequest would unshift an off-group model and
1674:  * the pin would no longer be strict (it could answer with a different model).
1675:  */
1676: export function resolveModelGroupCandidates(
1677:   memberDbIds: number[],
1678:   /**
1679:    * Members that were reached only through a group's auto-derived slug, not the
1680:    * id the client wrote (#651). They stay in the chain — resolution must never
1681:    * shrink — but as a strictly lower tier, so they can serve only once every
1682:    * literal match is exhausted. Omit it and every row is an equal candidate,
1683:    * which is what every other caller wants.
1684:    */
1685:   demotedDbIds?: ReadonlySet<number>,
1686: ): ChainRow[] {
1687:   const db = getDb();
1688:   const strategy = getRoutingStrategy();
1689:   if (strategy !== 'priority') refreshStatsCache(db);
1690: 
1691:   const activeProfileId = getActiveProfileId(db);
1692:   const selectMember = activeProfileId == null
1693:     ? db.prepare(`
1694:       SELECT m.id as model_db_id, COALESCE(fc.priority, 0) as priority,
1695:              1 as enabled,
1696:              m.platform, m.model_id, m.display_name, m.intelligence_rank,
1697:              m.size_label, m.monthly_token_budget,
1698:              m.rpm_limit, m.rpd_limit, m.tpm_limit, m.tpd_limit, m.supports_vision,
1699:              m.supports_tools, m.context_window, m.key_id, m.endpoint_scope
1700:       FROM models m
1701:       LEFT JOIN fallback_config fc ON fc.model_db_id = m.id
1702:       WHERE m.id = ? AND m.enabled = 1
1703:     `)
1704:     : db.prepare(`
1705:       SELECT m.id as model_db_id, COALESCE(pm.priority, fc.priority, 0) as priority,
1706:              1 as enabled,
1707:              m.platform, m.model_id, m.display_name, m.intelligence_rank,
1708:              m.size_label, m.monthly_token_budget,
1709:              m.rpm_limit, m.rpd_limit, m.tpm_limit, m.tpd_limit, m.supports_vision,
1710:              m.supports_tools, m.context_window, m.key_id, m.endpoint_scope
1711:       FROM models m
1712:       LEFT JOIN profile_models pm ON pm.profile_id = ? AND pm.model_db_id = m.id
1713:       LEFT JOIN fallback_config fc ON fc.model_db_id = m.id
1714:       WHERE m.id = ? AND m.enabled = 1
1715:     `);
1716: 
1717:   const rows: ChainRow[] = [];
1718:   for (const id of memberDbIds) {
1719:     const row = (activeProfileId == null ? selectMember.get(id) : selectMember.get(activeProfileId, id)) as ChainRow | undefined;
1720:     if (!row) continue;
1721:     row.match_tier = demotedDbIds?.has(id) ? 1 : 0;
1722:     rows.push(row);
1723:   }
1724:   return orderChain(rows, strategy);
1725: }

1727: // A panel candidate surfaced to the fusion layer: enough to pick a diverse set
1728: // and resolve each to a pinned dispatch.
1729: export interface FusionCandidate {
1730:   modelDbId: number;
1731:   platform: string;
1732:   modelId: string;
1733:   displayName: string;
1734:   sizeLabel: string;
1735:   supportsVision: number;
1736:   supportsTools: number;
1737: }
1738: 
1739: /**
1740:  * The active fallback chain ordered by the current routing strategy, surfaced
1741:  * for fusion panel selection. Same ordering the normal auto-router would walk,
1742:  * so the panel's auto-pick draws from the highest-scored models first and the
1743:  * fusion layer just needs to apply provider-diversity on top.
1744:  */
1745: export function getOrderedFusionChain(estimatedTokens: number, exactOutputReserve = 0): FusionCandidate[] {
1746:   const db = getDb();
1747:   const strategy = getRoutingStrategy();
1748:   if (strategy !== 'priority') refreshStatsCache(db);
1749:   const chain = getActiveChain(db).filter(e => e.enabled);
1750: 
1751:   // Only consider models that can ACTUALLY be served RIGHT NOW — applying the
1752:   // same gate selectKeyForModel uses when the router walks the chain: the model
1753:   // must have a key that is enabled + healthy, NOT on cooldown (e.g. a
1754:   // HuggingFace key benched for a day after a 402 "Payment Required"), within
1755:   // the provider's daily request cap, and under its per-minute/day request
1756:   // limits. Without this, a high-strategy-ranked model whose only key is
1757:   // currently cooled down (huggingface/Kimi-K2.6) would claim a panel slot it
1758:   // can't fill — surfacing as "no available key" and pushing out a usable model,
1759:   // which also makes the panel look like it's ignoring the routing strategy.
1760:   //
1761:   // The SIZE gates matter as much as the key gates: a model whose context window
1762:   // cannot hold the prompt can NEVER fill its slot, yet diversifyChain keeps
1763:   // handing it one on every request when it is its platform's only representative.
1764:   // That leaves one panel slot dead on arrival and reports the failure as the
1765:   // misleading "no available key for model". Passing a placeholder token count
1766:   // here made both size gates no-ops.
1767:   const usableKeys = db.prepare(
1768:     "SELECT id, platform, model_scope_json FROM api_keys WHERE enabled = 1 AND status IN ('healthy', 'unknown')"
1769:   ).all() as { id: number; platform: string; model_scope_json: string | null }[];
1770:   // Scope parsed once per key row (#657); the servable filter below re-checks
1771:   // membership per model.
1772:   const keysByPlatform = new Map<string, { id: number; scope: Set<string> | null }[]>();
1773:   for (const k of usableKeys) {
1774:     const entry = { id: k.id, scope: parseModelScope(k.model_scope_json) };
1775:     const arr = keysByPlatform.get(k.platform);
1776:     if (arr) arr.push(entry); else keysByPlatform.set(k.platform, [entry]);
1777:   }
1778:   // Soft preference (#956 review): prefer models whose window holds the estimate
1779:   // WITH the safety margin; /v1/models still advertises the raw window, so if
1780:   // NOTHING survives that pass, re-run allowing raw advertised-window fits
1781:   // rather than handing back an empty chain — a request packed to the
1782:   // advertised window keeps its one attempt (the mid-chain context_too_large
1783:   // 400 is classified and retried downstream).
1784:   const passesContextGate = (e: ChainRow, allowMarginViolators: boolean) => {
1785:     // A null context_window means "unknown", not "zero": same convention the
1786:     // auto-router uses, so an unspecified window is never itself a reason to skip.
1787:     if (fitsContextWindow(e.platform, e.context_window, estimatedTokens, exactOutputReserve)) return true;
1788:     return allowMarginViolators && fitsContextWindowStrict(e.context_window, estimatedTokens);
1789:   };
1790:   const servableFilter = (allowMarginViolators: boolean) => chain.filter(e => {
1791:     if (!passesContextGate(e, allowMarginViolators)) return false;
1792:     const keyIds = keysByPlatform.get(e.platform);
1793:     if (!keyIds) return false;
1794:     // Same endpoint-pool rule the router applies (#619).
1795:     const endpointKeyIds = e.platform === 'custom' && e.key_id != null
1796:       ? customEndpointKeyIds(db, e.key_id)
1797:       : null;
1798:     const limits = { rpm: e.rpm_limit, rpd: e.rpd_limit, tpm: e.tpm_limit, tpd: e.tpd_limit };
1799:     return keyIds.some(({ id: kid, scope }) =>
1800:       scopeAllows(scope, e.model_id) &&
1801:       (endpointKeyIds == null || endpointKeyIds.has(kid)) &&
1802:       !isOnCooldown(e.platform, e.model_id, kid) &&
1803:       canUseProvider(e.platform, kid) &&
1804:       canUseProviderMinute(e.platform, kid) &&
1805:       canMakeRequest(e.platform, e.model_id, kid, limits) &&
1806:       canUseProviderTokens(e.platform, kid, e.model_id, estimatedTokens),
1807:     );
1808:   });
1809:   let servable = servableFilter(false);
1810:   if (servable.length === 0) servable = servableFilter(true);
1811: 
1812:   // Deterministic (expected-score) ordering so the panel faithfully follows the
1813:   // user's picked routing strategy instead of re-sampling a fresh draw each call.
1814:   const ordered = orderChain(servable, strategy, false);
1815:   return ordered.map(e => ({
1816:     modelDbId: e.model_db_id,
1817:     platform: e.platform,
1818:     modelId: e.model_id,
1819:     displayName: e.display_name,
1820:     sizeLabel: e.size_label,
1821:     supportsVision: e.supports_vision,
1822:     supportsTools: e.supports_tools,
1823:   }));
1824: }

1826: /**
1827:  * Resolve an explicit model id (as a client would type it) to a fusion
1828:  * candidate, or null when it isn't a known enabled model. Prefers an enabled
1829:  * row; dedupes a model id that exists on multiple platforms by intelligence
1830:  * rank, matching how /v1/models picks a representative row.
1831:  */
1832: export function resolveFusionCandidate(modelId: string): FusionCandidate | null {
1833:   const db = getDb();
1834:   const row = db.prepare(`
1835:     SELECT m.id as model_db_id, m.platform, m.model_id, m.display_name,
1836:            m.size_label, m.supports_vision, m.supports_tools
1837:     FROM models m
1838:     WHERE m.model_id = ? AND m.enabled = 1
1839:     ORDER BY m.intelligence_rank ASC, m.id ASC
1840:     LIMIT 1
1841:   `).get(modelId) as {
1842:     model_db_id: number; platform: string; model_id: string; display_name: string;
1843:     size_label: string; supports_vision: number; supports_tools: number;
1844:   } | undefined;
1845:   if (row) {
1846:     return {
1847:       modelDbId: row.model_db_id,
1848:       platform: row.platform,
1849:       modelId: row.model_id,
1850:       displayName: row.display_name,
1851:       sizeLabel: row.size_label,
1852:       supportsVision: row.supports_vision,
1853:       supportsTools: row.supports_tools,
1854:     };
1855:   }
1856: 
1857:   // Unify ON: a fusion picker value may be a canonical GROUP id rather than a
1858:   // raw model_id. Resolve it to the group's best-ordered enabled member so
1859:   // saved fusion configs that use canonical ids keep working. Exact model_id
1860:   // match above always wins first, so OFF mode and legacy configs are untouched.
1861:   if (isUnifyEnabled()) {
1862:     const resolved = resolveRequestedIdForDispatch(modelId, getModelGroups());
1863:     if (resolved && resolved.memberDbIds.length > 0) {
1864:       const top = resolveModelGroupCandidates(resolved.memberDbIds, resolved.demotedDbIds)[0];
1865:       if (top) {
1866:         return {
1867:           modelDbId: top.model_db_id,
1868:           platform: top.platform,
1869:           modelId: top.model_id,
1870:           displayName: top.display_name,
1871:           sizeLabel: top.size_label,
1872:           supportsVision: top.supports_vision,
1873:           supportsTools: top.supports_tools,
1874:         };
1875:       }
1876:     }
1877:   }
1878:   return null;
1879: }

1881: export function routeRequest(estimatedTokens = 1000, skipKeys?: Set<string>, preferredModelDbId?: number, requireVision = false, requireTools = false, skipModels?: Set<number>, prefetchedChain?: ChainRow[], requireStructured = false, skipPlatforms?: Set<string>, exactOutputReserve = 0): RouteResult {
1882:   const db = getDb();
1883: 
1884:   const strategy = getRoutingStrategy();
1885:   if (strategy !== 'priority') refreshStatsCache(db);
1886: 
1887:   const chain = (prefetchedChain ?? getActiveChain(db)).filter(e => e.enabled);
1888: 
1889:   const sortedChain = orderChain(chain, strategy);
1890: 
1891:   // Exploration toggle (#685/#707 follow-up): when enabled, give a model with
1892:   // no reliability/speed samples a guaranteed chance to be tried, so it stops
1893:   // losing every bandit draw to prior-heavy rivals. With EXPLORE_CHANCE
1894:   // probability, pick one unmeasured model uniformly and try it first; if it
1895:   // fails, the loop falls through to the scored order as usual. Only for
1896:   // bandit strategies — Manual is the operator's explicit order.
1897:   // Candidates the main loop would immediately reject for THIS request are
1898:   // excluded up front (ruled-out models plus the request-level capability
1899:   // gates: vision/tools/structured output/context window): promoting a model
1900:   // that can't serve the request ahead of capable ones would just get it
1901:   // skipped a moment later (e.g. an image request must never randomly probe a
1902:   // text-only model).
1903:   // While the gateway is in degraded mode (#904) exploration is skipped
1904:   // entirely: probing unmeasured models during a fleet-wide outage just burns
1905:   // retry budget on the same dead providers, and the scored order of known
1906:   // survivors is the only thing worth trying.
1907:   if (strategy !== 'priority' && getExploreEnabled() && !isDegraded() && Math.random() < EXPLORE_CHANCE) {
1908:     // A model the operator zeroed out via MODEL_ROUTING_OVERRIDES never wins a
1909:     // bandit draw, so it would stay under EXPLORE_MIN_SAMPLES forever and become
1910:     // a perpetual probe target — the explicit ban outranks exploration.
1911:     const overrides = getModelWeightOverrides();
1912:     const unmeasured = sortedChain.filter(e => {
1913:       if (overrides.get(e.model_id) === 0) return false;
1914:       const stats = statsCache?.get(modelStatsKey(e.platform, e.model_id, e.endpoint_scope));
1915:       if ((stats?.successes ?? 0) + (stats?.failures ?? 0) >= EXPLORE_MIN_SAMPLES) return false;
1916:       // Mirror the main loop's gates below so exploration only samples
1917:       // candidates that can actually serve this request.
1918:       if (skipModels?.has(e.model_db_id)) return false;
1919:       if (skipPlatforms?.has(e.platform)) return false;
1920:       if (requireVision && !e.supports_vision) return false;
1921:       if (requireTools && !e.supports_tools) return false;
1922:       if (requireStructured && platformDropsResponseFormat(e.platform)) return false;
1923:       if (!fitsContextWindow(e.platform, e.context_window, estimatedTokens, exactOutputReserve)) return false;
1924:       if (e.tpm_limit != null && estimatedTokens > e.tpm_limit) return false;
1925:       return true;
1926:     });
1927:     if (unmeasured.length > 0) {
1928:       const probe = unmeasured[Math.floor(Math.random() * unmeasured.length)];
1929:       const idx = sortedChain.findIndex(e => e.model_db_id === probe.model_db_id);
1930:       if (idx > 0) {
1931:         const [probeRow] = sortedChain.splice(idx, 1);
1932:         sortedChain.unshift(probeRow);
1933:       }
1934:     }
1935:   }
1936: 
1937:   // Sticky session / Explicit pinning: move preferred model to front of chain
1938:   if (preferredModelDbId) {
1939:     const idx = sortedChain.findIndex(e => e.model_db_id === preferredModelDbId);
1940:     if (idx >= 0) {
1941:       if (idx > 0) {
1942:         const [preferred] = sortedChain.splice(idx, 1);
1943:         sortedChain.unshift(preferred);
1944:       }
1945:     } else {
1946:       // The requested model is not in the current routing chain (e.g. it's a
1947:       // custom model or not added to the active profile). We must fulfill the
1948:       // explicit request by injecting it at the front.
1949:       const pinnedRow = db.prepare(`
1950:         SELECT m.id as model_db_id, 0 as priority, 1 as enabled,
1951:                m.platform, m.model_id, m.display_name, m.intelligence_rank,
1952:                m.size_label, m.monthly_token_budget,
1953:                m.rpm_limit, m.rpd_limit, m.tpm_limit, m.tpd_limit, m.supports_vision,
1954:                m.supports_tools, m.context_window, m.key_id, m.endpoint_scope
1955:         FROM models m
1956:         WHERE m.id = ? AND m.enabled = 1
1957:       `).get(preferredModelDbId) as ChainRow | undefined;
1958:       
1959:       if (pinnedRow) {
1960:         sortedChain.unshift(pinnedRow);
1961:       }
1962:     }
1963:   }
1964: 
1965:   // Per-model disposition, attached to the exhaustion error when the loop falls
1966:   // through with no route — the only record of WHY the pool was empty on the
1967:   // synchronous "all exhausted" path (nothing downstream logs it). See issue _1.
1968:   const diag: string[] = [];
1969: 
1970:   // Margin as a SOFT preference (#956 review): /v1/models advertises the raw
1971:   // window, so clients legitimately pack requests right up to it — excluding
1972:   // those models outright turned an already-handled upstream 400 into "all
1973:   // models exhausted" with zero attempts. Keep the operator's order intact but
1974:   // sweep margin-fitting models first; ones that only fit the advertised window
1975:   // stay eligible behind them. Worst case is one classified context_too_large
1976:   // hop instead of no route at all.
1977:   const servingChain: ChainRow[] = [];
1978:   const marginDeferred: ChainRow[] = [];
1979:   for (const e of sortedChain) {
1980:     (fitsContextWindow(e.platform, e.context_window, estimatedTokens, exactOutputReserve) ? servingChain : marginDeferred).push(e);
1981:   }
1982:   servingChain.push(...marginDeferred);
1983: 
1984:   for (const entry of servingChain) {
1985:     const label = `${entry.platform}/${entry.model_id}`;
1986:     // Models the caller has ruled out for this request — e.g. a 404
1987:     // "model removed upstream" already seen this request: trying the same
1988:     // model again on a different key would just burn another attempt on the
1989:     // same dead route (PR #111, credits @barbotkonv).
1990:     if (skipModels?.has(entry.model_db_id)) { diag.push(`${label}: ruled out earlier this request`); continue; }
1991: 
1992:     // Platforms the caller has ruled out wholesale (#788): a provider-level
1993:     // failure this request — a 5xx, a timeout, a dead socket — is about the
1994:     // PROVIDER, so its other keys and its other models would fail the same way.
1995:     // Skipping the platform moves failover to the next provider instead of
1996:     // burning one hop per key. Request-scoped; nothing is benched by this.
1997:     if (skipPlatforms?.has(entry.platform)) { diag.push(`${label}: provider ruled out earlier this request`); continue; }
1998: 
1999:     // Vision requests skip text-only models — including a sticky/preferred one,
2000:     // which is correct: don't pin an image turn to a model that can't see it.
2001:     if (requireVision && !entry.supports_vision) { diag.push(`${label}: no vision support`); continue; }
2002: 
2003:     // Tool-bearing requests skip models that can't emit structured tool_calls.
2004:     // A model that "answers" a tool request with the call serialized as text
2005:     // looks successful at the transport level while the client's harness sees
2006:     // nothing — worse than a failover. Applies to sticky models too, same
2007:     // reasoning as vision above.
2008:     if (requireTools && !entry.supports_tools) { diag.push(`${label}: no tool-calling support`); continue; }
2009: 
2010:     // Structured-output routing (#514 follow-up): when the request carries a
2011:     // response_format, skip platforms whose param policy can't even receive it
2012:     // (the param would be dropped before send, so the model would answer in
2013:     // prose and burn a failover hop). Platform-level fast path — model-level
2014:     // capability isn't in the catalog; models that accept the param but ignore
2015:     // it are caught by the non-stream JSON enforcement downstream.
2016:     if (requireStructured && platformDropsResponseFormat(entry.platform)) { diag.push(`${label}: platform drops response_format`); continue; }
2017: 
2018:     // Context-aware routing fast path (#167): skip a model whose RAW advertised
2019:     // window cannot hold the request — a dispatch there is a guaranteed 413.
2020:     // Margin-violating-but-raw-fitting models are NOT skipped (soft preference,
2021:     // #956 review): they were merely deferred to the back of the sweep above.
2022:     // estimatedTokens is the INPUT estimate plus a CAPPED output reserve
2023:     // (routingReserveTokens, #470), so a huge client-set max_tokens no longer
2024:     // excludes the model — the input must fit, not input+full max_tokens. A 413
2025:     // that slips through is still retryable downstream, and the failed model is
2026:     // put on cooldown — so this is a fast-path, not the only guard. If every
2027:     // model is too small, the loop falls through and the caller gets the normal
2028:     // "all models exhausted" error rather than a wasted sweep.
2029:     if (!fitsContextWindowStrict(entry.context_window, estimatedTokens)) {
2030:       // Keep the `< estimated` substring — summarizeExhaustion buckets prompt
2031:       // overflow off it. Emit the EFFECTIVE number so the line doesn't read as
2032:       // false (#956 review): e.g. `context 131072 < estimated 106000 x1.25 = 132500`.
2033:       const reserve = Math.max(0, exactOutputReserve);
2034:       const requiredWithMargin = Math.ceil(Math.max(0, estimatedTokens - reserve) * CONTEXT_WINDOW_SAFETY_FACTOR + reserve);
2035:       diag.push(TRIM_GUARDED_PLATFORMS.has(entry.platform)
2036:         ? `${label}: context ${entry.context_window} < estimated ${estimatedTokens}`
2037:         : `${label}: context ${entry.context_window} < estimated ${estimatedTokens} x${CONTEXT_WINDOW_SAFETY_FACTOR} = ${requiredWithMargin}`);
2038:       continue;
2039:     }
2040: 
2041:     // Same guard for a model with a small per-minute token budget: a request
2042:     // whose input alone exceeds tpm_limit can never fit one minute of quota and
2043:     // returns a guaranteed 413 (e.g. Groq gpt-oss-120b: 131k context but 8k TPM).
2044:     // estimatedTokens carries the same capped output reserve, mirroring the
2045:     // check above (#470).
2046:     if (entry.tpm_limit != null && estimatedTokens > entry.tpm_limit) { diag.push(`${label}: tpm_limit ${entry.tpm_limit} < estimated ${estimatedTokens}`); continue; }
2047: 
2048:     // Key selection + accounting pre-checks for this one model. Returns the
2049:     // first usable key's RouteResult, or null when the model has no key that
