1377:   const keys = allKeys.filter(k => scopeAllows(parseModelScope(k.model_scope_json), entry.model_id));
1378:   if (keys.length === 0) {
1379:     diag?.push(`${label}: no usable key — ${allKeys.length} key(s) scoped to other models`);
1380:     return null;
1381:   }
1382: 
1383:   // Tally the gate that rejected each key, so the exhaustion diagnostic can say
1384:   // *why* a model with keys still couldn't serve (all on cooldown vs over quota).
1385:   const skipTally: Record<string, number> = {};
1386:   const note = (reason: string) => { skipTally[reason] = (skipTally[reason] ?? 0) + 1; };
1387: 
1388:   const limits = {
1389:     rpm: entry.rpm_limit,
1390:     rpd: entry.rpd_limit,
1391:     tpm: entry.tpm_limit,
1392:     tpd: entry.tpd_limit,
1393:   };
1394: 
1395:   // Score-ordered walk over this model's keys (#580): when any key has recorded
1396:   // reliability/speed data, try them best-sampled-score first so a chronically
1397:   // failing key stops soaking up every Nth request. The stats cache is the same
1398:   // 60s-TTL aggregate the model-level bandit uses (refresh is a no-op when
1399:   // fresh, and cheap when not). With no data at all, keep the legacy rotation.
1400:   refreshStatsCache(db);
1401:   // Scoped so two relays offering the same model id don't share one rotation
1402:   // cursor over the platform's key list (#651).
1403:   const rrKey = modelStatsKey(entry.platform, entry.model_id, entry.endpoint_scope);
1404:   let idx = roundRobinIndex.get(rrKey) ?? 0;
1405:   let ranked = orderKeysByScore(entry, keys);
1406: 
1407:   // Remaining-quota weighting (#919) layers on top: it re-sorts whatever order
1408:   // we were going to walk anyway — the bandit ranking when there is per-key
1409:   // data, otherwise the round-robin rotation starting at the live cursor — so
1410:   // ties fall back to that order instead of to rowid.
1411:   if (keys.length > 1 && quotaWeightingApplies(entry)) {
1412:     const base = ranked ?? Array.from({ length: keys.length }, (_, i) => keys[(idx + i) % keys.length]);
1413:     ranked = orderKeysByRemainingQuota(entry, base);
1414:   }
1415: 
1416:   // A custom model belongs to exactly one endpoint (#212), but an endpoint can
1417:   // hold several credentials — so the pool is every key on the same base_url,
1418:   // rotated like any other platform's keys (#619). Legacy rows (key_id NULL)
1419:   // keep the old any-key match.
1420:   const endpointKeyIds = entry.platform === 'custom' && entry.key_id != null
1421:     ? customEndpointKeyIds(db, entry.key_id)
1422:     : null;
1423: 
1424:   for (let attempt = 0; attempt < keys.length; attempt++) {
1425:     const key = ranked ? ranked[attempt] : keys[idx % keys.length];
1426:     idx++;
1427: 
1428:     if (endpointKeyIds && !endpointKeyIds.has(key.id)) { note('custom-key-mismatch'); continue; }
1429: 
1430:     const skipId = `${entry.platform}:${entry.model_id}:${key.id}`;
1431:     if (skipKeys?.has(skipId)) { note('already-failed-this-request'); continue; }
1432: 
1433:     if (isOnCooldown(entry.platform, entry.model_id, key.id)) { note('cooldown'); continue; }
1434:     if (!canUseProvider(entry.platform, key.id)) { note('provider-daily-cap'); continue; }
1435:     // Account-wide per-minute budget, checked before the per-model gates: a model
1436:     // with a NULL rpm_limit would otherwise sail past them and spend a budget its
1437:     // siblings share.
1438:     if (!canUseProviderMinute(entry.platform, key.id)) { note('provider-minute-cap'); continue; }
1439:     // Skip a key that already has its allowed requests in the air. Without this,
1440:     // parallel streams all pick the same key and 429 each other on providers that
1441:     // meter concurrency per credential.
1442:     if (!canUseKeyConcurrency(entry.platform, key.id)) { note('key-concurrency'); continue; }
1443:     if (!canMakeRequest(entry.platform, entry.model_id, key.id, limits)) { note('rpm/rpd-limit'); continue; }
1444:     if (!canUseTokens(entry.platform, entry.model_id, key.id, estimatedTokens, limits)) { note('tpm/tpd-limit'); continue; }
1445:     if (!canUseProviderTokens(entry.platform, key.id, entry.model_id, estimatedTokens)) { note('provider-daily-token-cap'); continue; }
1446: 
1447:     let decryptedKey: string;
1448:     try {
1449:       decryptedKey = decrypt(key.encrypted_key, key.iv, key.auth_tag);
1450:     } catch {
1451:       db.prepare("UPDATE api_keys SET status = 'error', last_checked_at = datetime('now') WHERE id = ?")
1452:         .run(key.id);
1453:       note('decrypt-error');
1454:       continue;
1455:     }
1456: 
1457:     const resolvedProvider = entry.platform === 'custom'
1458:       ? resolveProvider('custom', key.base_url)
1459:       : provider;
1460:     if (!resolvedProvider) { note('no-resolved-provider'); continue; }
1461: 
1462:     roundRobinIndex.set(rrKey, idx);
1463:     // Taken only once the key has cleared every gate and is definitely being
1464:     // returned, so a rejected candidate never consumes concurrency budget.
1465:     const leaseId = acquireLease(entry.platform, entry.model_id, key.id, estimatedTokens);
1466:     return {
1467:       provider: resolvedProvider,
1468:       modelId: entry.model_id,
1469:       modelDbId: entry.model_db_id,
1470:       apiKey: decryptedKey,
1471:       keyId: key.id,
1472:       keyLabel: key.label || null,
1473:       // Decrypted once here, at the point the row is already in hand (#590).
1474:       proxyUrl: decryptProxyUrl(key),
1475:       platform: entry.platform,
1476:       displayName: entry.display_name,
1477:       endpointScope: entry.endpoint_scope ?? '',
1478:       rpdLimit: limits.rpd,
1479:       tpdLimit: limits.tpd,
1480:       release: () => releaseLease(leaseId),
1481:     };
1482:   }
1483: 
1484:   // No usable key for this model. Advance the round-robin index anyway so we
1485:   // don't get stuck re-trying the same exhausted key first next time.
1486:   roundRobinIndex.set(rrKey, idx);
1487:   const summary = Object.entries(skipTally).map(([r, n]) => `${r}:${n}`).join(', ') || 'no usable key';
1488:   diag?.push(`${label}: ${keys.length} key(s) — ${summary}`);
1489:   return null;
1490: }
1491: 
1492: /**
1493:  * Whether the model still has ANOTHER key that could serve it right now, given
1494:  * the key that just failed (excludingKeyId) and any keys already ruled out this
1495:  * request (skipKeys, in the "platform:modelId:keyId" form). Applies the same
1496:  * gates selectKeyForModel uses — enabled + healthy status, not on cooldown,
1497:  * under the provider daily cap, and under rpm/rpd/tpm/tpd — so the answer means
1498:  * "a real, dispatchable alternative exists".
1499:  *
1500:  * Used by the retry loops to decide whether a single key's 429 should demote the
1501:  * WHOLE model (the model-level 429 penalty). It should not: the per-key cooldown
1502:  * already isolates the failing key, so demoting the model while a sibling key can
1503:  * still serve it wrongly sinks a healthy model in the scorer (#454). We only
1504:  * record the model-level hit when this returns false — i.e. the 429 exhausted the
1505:  * model, not just one of its keys.
1506:  */
1507: export function hasOtherUsableKey(modelDbId: number, excludingKeyId: number, skipKeys?: Set<string>): boolean {
1508:   const db = getDb();
1509:   const m = db.prepare(`
1510:     SELECT platform, model_id, rpm_limit, rpd_limit, tpm_limit, tpd_limit, key_id
1511:       FROM models WHERE id = ?
1512:   `).get(modelDbId) as {
1513:     platform: string; model_id: string;
1514:     rpm_limit: number | null; rpd_limit: number | null;
1515:     tpm_limit: number | null; tpd_limit: number | null; key_id: number | null;
1516:   } | undefined;
1517:   if (!m) return false;
1518: 
1519:   const limits = { rpm: m.rpm_limit, rpd: m.rpd_limit, tpm: m.tpm_limit, tpd: m.tpd_limit };
1520:   const keys = db.prepare(
1521:     "SELECT id, model_scope_json FROM api_keys WHERE platform = ? AND enabled = 1 AND status IN ('healthy', 'unknown')"
1522:   ).all(m.platform) as { id: number; model_scope_json: string | null }[];
1523: 
1524:   // Keys of the model's own custom endpoint (#212, #619); a key belonging to a
1525:   // DIFFERENT endpoint cannot serve it, so it doesn't count as an alternative.
1526:   const endpointKeyIds = m.platform === 'custom' && m.key_id != null
1527:     ? customEndpointKeyIds(db, m.key_id)
1528:     : null;
1529: 
1530:   for (const k of keys) {
1531:     if (k.id === excludingKeyId) continue;
1532:     if (endpointKeyIds && !endpointKeyIds.has(k.id)) continue;
1533:     // A sibling scoped away from this model can never serve it (#657) — counting
1534:     // it would wrongly suppress the model-level penalty this gate exists for.
1535:     if (!scopeAllows(parseModelScope(k.model_scope_json), m.model_id)) continue;
1536:     if (skipKeys?.has(`${m.platform}:${m.model_id}:${k.id}`)) continue;
1537:     if (isOnCooldown(m.platform, m.model_id, k.id)) continue;
1538:     if (!canUseProvider(m.platform, k.id)) continue;
1539:     if (!canUseProviderMinute(m.platform, k.id)) continue;
1540:     if (!canMakeRequest(m.platform, m.model_id, k.id, limits)) continue;
1541:     // A per-minute token spike on the failed key doesn't mean a fresh key lacks
1542:     // headroom; a nominal 1-token probe only rules out a key already at its
1543:     // TPM/TPD ceiling.
1544:     if (!canUseTokens(m.platform, m.model_id, k.id, 1, limits)) continue;
1545:     if (!canUseProviderTokens(m.platform, k.id, m.model_id, 1)) continue;
1546:     return true;
1547:   }
1548:   return false;
1549: }
1550: 
1551: /**
1552:  * Every key that can be ROUTED to this model: enabled + healthy/unknown, not
1553:  * scoped away from the model (#657), and — for a custom model — belonging to
1554:  * the model's own endpoint (#212, #619). Deliberately ignores the transient
1555:  * gates hasOtherUsableKey applies (cooldown, quotas): the caller here is the
1556:  * model-level bench, which needs the full key set to take a sick model out of
1557:  * rotation, not "who could serve the next request".
1558:  */
1559: export function routableKeyIdsForModel(modelDbId: number): number[] {
1560:   const db = getDb();
1561:   const m = db.prepare('SELECT platform, model_id, key_id FROM models WHERE id = ?')
1562:     .get(modelDbId) as { platform: string; model_id: string; key_id: number | null } | undefined;
1563:   if (!m) return [];
1564: 
1565:   const keys = db.prepare(
1566:     "SELECT id, model_scope_json FROM api_keys WHERE platform = ? AND enabled = 1 AND status IN ('healthy', 'unknown')"
1567:   ).all(m.platform) as { id: number; model_scope_json: string | null }[];
1568: 
1569:   const endpointKeyIds = m.platform === 'custom' && m.key_id != null
1570:     ? customEndpointKeyIds(db, m.key_id)
1571:     : null;
1572: 
1573:   return keys
1574:     .filter(k => !endpointKeyIds || endpointKeyIds.has(k.id))
1575:     .filter(k => scopeAllows(parseModelScope(k.model_scope_json), m.model_id))
1576:     .map(k => k.id);
1577: }

1579: /**
1580:  * Fetch a single enabled model's chain row by its db id.
1581:  */
1582: function getModelChainRow(db: Db, modelDbId: number): ChainRow | undefined {
1583:   return db.prepare(`
1584:     SELECT m.id as model_db_id, 0 as priority, 1 as enabled,
1585:            m.platform, m.model_id, m.display_name, m.intelligence_rank,
1586:            m.size_label, m.monthly_token_budget,
1587:            m.rpm_limit, m.rpd_limit, m.tpm_limit, m.tpd_limit, m.supports_vision,
1588:            m.supports_tools, m.context_window, m.key_id, m.endpoint_scope
1589:     FROM models m
1590:     WHERE m.id = ? AND m.enabled = 1
1591:   `).get(modelDbId) as ChainRow | undefined;
1592: }

1594: /**
1595:  * Safety margin applied when ranking a model against an estimated request size.
1596:  * The estimate is a chars/4 heuristic that under-counts dense payloads (JSON,
1597:  * code, CJK) by up to ~2x; without any accounting for that gap such requests
1598:  * were routed to models whose real tokenizer count exceeded the window and the
1599:  * provider rejected them with a 400 mid-chain (kilo: "maximum context length is
1600:  * 262144 tokens" on requests estimated <=256000).
1601:  *
1602:  * The margin is a SOFT preference, not a hard filter (#956 review): /v1/models
1603:  * advertises the RAW window, so clients legitimately pack requests right up to
1604:  * it. Excluding margin-violating models outright would turn an upstream 400
1605:  * that the retry loop already classifies and handles (`context_too_large`)
1606:  * into a regression: "all models exhausted" with zero attempts. Callers
1607:  * therefore try margin-fitting candidates first and only fall back to raw
1608:  * advertised-window fits (see fitsContextWindowStrict) when nothing else can
1609:  * serve the request.
1610:  */
1611: export const CONTEXT_WINDOW_SAFETY_FACTOR = 1.25;
1612: 
1613: // Platforms whose pre-dispatch trim guard already caps the dispatched input
1614: // below the live context ceiling (lib/content.ts truncateMessagesForGithub):
1615: // the guard — not the routing estimate — is what guarantees the fit there, so
1616: // applying the factor too would only make that guard unreachable. The margin
1617: // checks below treat these platforms as strict comparisons.
1618: const TRIM_GUARDED_PLATFORMS = new Set(['github']);
1619: 
1620: /** True when `estimatedTokens` fits the RAW advertised window (null window =
1621:  * unknown, never filtered — same convention as the auto-router). This is the
1622:  * comparison /v1/models publishes and the soft-preference fallback tier. */
1623: export function fitsContextWindowStrict(contextWindow: number | null | undefined, estimatedTokens: number): boolean {
1624:   return contextWindow == null || estimatedTokens <= contextWindow;
1625: }
1626: 
1627: /** True when `estimatedTokens` plausibly fits `contextWindow` WITH the safety
1628:  * margin. The chars/4 heuristic portion is scaled by the factor; an explicit
1629:  * output reserve derived from the client's max_tokens (`routingReserveTokens`)
1630:  * is already an exact count and is added UNSCALED (#956 review). Trim-guarded
1631:  * platforms compare strictly — their guard guarantees the fit. */
1632: export function fitsContextWindow(platform: string, contextWindow: number | null | undefined, estimatedTokens: number, exactOutputReserve = 0): boolean {
1633:   if (contextWindow == null) return true;
1634:   // Raw advertised comparison first — the margin can only shrink eligibility.
1635:   if (estimatedTokens > contextWindow) return false;
1636:   if (TRIM_GUARDED_PLATFORMS.has(platform)) return true;
1637:   const reserve = Math.max(0, exactOutputReserve);
1638:   const heuristic = Math.max(0, estimatedTokens - reserve);
1639:   return heuristic * CONTEXT_WINDOW_SAFETY_FACTOR + reserve <= contextWindow;
1640: }
1641: 
1642: /**
1643:  * Route to ONE specific model, hard-pinned. Rotates across that model's keys
1644:  * (cooldowns, quotas, decryption all honored) but NEVER substitutes a different
1645:  * model — returns null if the pinned model can't serve right now. This is what
1646:  * makes a fusion panel genuinely diverse: a rate-limited slot is dropped, not
1647:  * silently collapsed onto whatever else is available. `skipKeys` lets a slot
1648:  * exclude keys it already failed on this request.
1649:  */
1650: export function routePinnedModel(modelDbId: number, estimatedTokens = 1000, skipKeys?: Set<string>): RouteResult | null {
1651:   const db = getDb();
1652:   const entry = getModelChainRow(db, modelDbId);
1653:   if (!entry) return null;
1654:   // Strict comparison only (#956 review): a pinned slot has no substitute, so
1655:   // refusing on a margin violation would drop the slot outright where the
1656:   // pre-margin behavior was one dispatch attempt (a mid-chain context_too_large
1657:   // 400 is classified and retried downstream). Nothing is multiplied here —
1658:   // estimatedTokens already carries the exact capped output reserve (#470).
1659:   if (!fitsContextWindowStrict(entry.context_window, estimatedTokens)) return null;
1660:   if (entry.tpm_limit != null && estimatedTokens > entry.tpm_limit) return null;
1661:   return selectKeyForModel(entry, estimatedTokens, skipKeys);
1662: }
1663: 
1664: /**
1665:  * Resolve a logical model group's member db ids to an ordered ChainRow[] for
1666:  * strict group-pin routing (the "unify" feature). Each catalog-enabled member
1667:  * is hydrated as a ChainRow carrying its active-profile/manual priority, then
1668:  * ordered by the active strategy via orderChain. Auto-chain enabled/disabled is
1669:  * intentionally ignored here because an explicit model request should still be
1670:  * able to use a direct model that the user removed from auto routing.
1671:  *
1672:  * Pass the result to routeRequest() as `prefetchedChain` and DO NOT pass a
1673:  * `preferredModelDbId` that isn't already one of these rows — otherwise the
1674:  * preferred-model injection in routeRequest would unshift an off-group model and
1675:  * the pin would no longer be strict (it could answer with a different model).
1676:  */
1677: export function resolveModelGroupCandidates(
1678:   memberDbIds: number[],
1679:   /**
1680:    * Members that were reached only through a group's auto-derived slug, not the
1681:    * id the client wrote (#651). They stay in the chain — resolution must never
1682:    * shrink — but as a strictly lower tier, so they can serve only once every
1683:    * literal match is exhausted. Omit it and every row is an equal candidate,
1684:    * which is what every other caller wants.
1685:    */
1686:   demotedDbIds?: ReadonlySet<number>,
1687: ): ChainRow[] {
1688:   const db = getDb();
1689:   const strategy = getRoutingStrategy();
1690:   if (strategy !== 'priority') refreshStatsCache(db);
1691: 
1692:   const activeProfileId = getActiveProfileId(db);
1693:   const selectMember = activeProfileId == null
1694:     ? db.prepare(`
1695:       SELECT m.id as model_db_id, COALESCE(fc.priority, 0) as priority,
1696:              1 as enabled,
1697:              m.platform, m.model_id, m.display_name, m.intelligence_rank,
1698:              m.size_label, m.monthly_token_budget,
1699:              m.rpm_limit, m.rpd_limit, m.tpm_limit, m.tpd_limit, m.supports_vision,
1700:              m.supports_tools, m.context_window, m.key_id, m.endpoint_scope
1701:       FROM models m
1702:       LEFT JOIN fallback_config fc ON fc.model_db_id = m.id
1703:       WHERE m.id = ? AND m.enabled = 1
1704:     `)
1705:     : db.prepare(`
1706:       SELECT m.id as model_db_id, COALESCE(pm.priority, fc.priority, 0) as priority,
1707:              1 as enabled,
1708:              m.platform, m.model_id, m.display_name, m.intelligence_rank,
1709:              m.size_label, m.monthly_token_budget,
1710:              m.rpm_limit, m.rpd_limit, m.tpm_limit, m.tpd_limit, m.supports_vision,
1711:              m.supports_tools, m.context_window, m.key_id, m.endpoint_scope
1712:       FROM models m
1713:       LEFT JOIN profile_models pm ON pm.profile_id = ? AND pm.model_db_id = m.id
1714:       LEFT JOIN fallback_config fc ON fc.model_db_id = m.id
1715:       WHERE m.id = ? AND m.enabled = 1
1716:     `);
1717: 
1718:   const rows: ChainRow[] = [];
1719:   for (const id of memberDbIds) {
1720:     const row = (activeProfileId == null ? selectMember.get(id) : selectMember.get(activeProfileId, id)) as ChainRow | undefined;
1721:     if (!row) continue;
1722:     row.match_tier = demotedDbIds?.has(id) ? 1 : 0;
1723:     rows.push(row);
1724:   }
1725:   return orderChain(rows, strategy);
1726: }

1728: // A panel candidate surfaced to the fusion layer: enough to pick a diverse set
1729: // and resolve each to a pinned dispatch.
1730: export interface FusionCandidate {
1731:   modelDbId: number;
1732:   platform: string;
1733:   modelId: string;
1734:   displayName: string;
1735:   sizeLabel: string;
1736:   supportsVision: number;
1737:   supportsTools: number;
1738: }
1739: 
1740: /**
1741:  * The active fallback chain ordered by the current routing strategy, surfaced
1742:  * for fusion panel selection. Same ordering the normal auto-router would walk,
1743:  * so the panel's auto-pick draws from the highest-scored models first and the
1744:  * fusion layer just needs to apply provider-diversity on top.
1745:  */
1746: export function getOrderedFusionChain(estimatedTokens: number, exactOutputReserve = 0): FusionCandidate[] {
1747:   const db = getDb();
1748:   const strategy = getRoutingStrategy();
1749:   if (strategy !== 'priority') refreshStatsCache(db);
1750:   const chain = getActiveChain(db).filter(e => e.enabled);
1751: 
1752:   // Only consider models that can ACTUALLY be served RIGHT NOW — applying the
1753:   // same gate selectKeyForModel uses when the router walks the chain: the model
1754:   // must have a key that is enabled + healthy, NOT on cooldown (e.g. a
1755:   // HuggingFace key benched for a day after a 402 "Payment Required"), within
1756:   // the provider's daily request cap, and under its per-minute/day request
1757:   // limits. Without this, a high-strategy-ranked model whose only key is
1758:   // currently cooled down (huggingface/Kimi-K2.6) would claim a panel slot it
1759:   // can't fill — surfacing as "no available key" and pushing out a usable model,
1760:   // which also makes the panel look like it's ignoring the routing strategy.
1761:   //
1762:   // The SIZE gates matter as much as the key gates: a model whose context window
1763:   // cannot hold the prompt can NEVER fill its slot, yet diversifyChain keeps
1764:   // handing it one on every request when it is its platform's only representative.
1765:   // That leaves one panel slot dead on arrival and reports the failure as the
1766:   // misleading "no available key for model". Passing a placeholder token count
1767:   // here made both size gates no-ops.
1768:   const usableKeys = db.prepare(
1769:     "SELECT id, platform, model_scope_json FROM api_keys WHERE enabled = 1 AND status IN ('healthy', 'unknown')"
1770:   ).all() as { id: number; platform: string; model_scope_json: string | null }[];
1771:   // Scope parsed once per key row (#657); the servable filter below re-checks
1772:   // membership per model.
1773:   const keysByPlatform = new Map<string, { id: number; scope: Set<string> | null }[]>();
1774:   for (const k of usableKeys) {
1775:     const entry = { id: k.id, scope: parseModelScope(k.model_scope_json) };
1776:     const arr = keysByPlatform.get(k.platform);
1777:     if (arr) arr.push(entry); else keysByPlatform.set(k.platform, [entry]);
1778:   }
1779:   // Soft preference (#956 review): prefer models whose window holds the estimate
1780:   // WITH the safety margin; /v1/models still advertises the raw window, so if
1781:   // NOTHING survives that pass, re-run allowing raw advertised-window fits
1782:   // rather than handing back an empty chain — a request packed to the
1783:   // advertised window keeps its one attempt (the mid-chain context_too_large
1784:   // 400 is classified and retried downstream).
1785:   const passesContextGate = (e: ChainRow, allowMarginViolators: boolean) => {
1786:     // A null context_window means "unknown", not "zero": same convention the
1787:     // auto-router uses, so an unspecified window is never itself a reason to skip.
1788:     if (fitsContextWindow(e.platform, e.context_window, estimatedTokens, exactOutputReserve)) return true;
1789:     return allowMarginViolators && fitsContextWindowStrict(e.context_window, estimatedTokens);
1790:   };
1791:   const servableFilter = (allowMarginViolators: boolean) => chain.filter(e => {
1792:     if (!passesContextGate(e, allowMarginViolators)) return false;
1793:     const keyIds = keysByPlatform.get(e.platform);
1794:     if (!keyIds) return false;
1795:     // Same endpoint-pool rule the router applies (#619).
1796:     const endpointKeyIds = e.platform === 'custom' && e.key_id != null
1797:       ? customEndpointKeyIds(db, e.key_id)
1798:       : null;
1799:     const limits = { rpm: e.rpm_limit, rpd: e.rpd_limit, tpm: e.tpm_limit, tpd: e.tpd_limit };
1800:     return keyIds.some(({ id: kid, scope }) =>

93:   const bump = (bucket: string) => { counts[bucket] = (counts[bucket] ?? 0) + 1; };
94:   for (const line of diag) {
95:     const l = line.toLowerCase();
96:     if (l.includes('no provider registered')) bump('unsupported provider');
97:     else if (/no enabled\+healthy key|no usable key|decrypt-error/.test(l)) bump('no usable key configured');
98:     else if (l.includes('< estimated')) bump('prompt too large for the model');
99:     else if (l.includes('no vision support')) bump('model lacks vision');
100:     else if (l.includes('no tool-calling support')) bump('model lacks tool-calling');
101:     else if (l.includes('drops response_format')) bump('platform cannot honor response_format');
102:     else if (/ruled out|already-failed/.test(l)) bump('failed earlier this request');
103:     else if (/cooldown|rpm|rpd|tpm|tpd|provider-daily-cap/.test(l)) bump('rate-limited or on cooldown');
104:     else bump('unavailable');
105:   }
106:   // Most actionable buckets first.
107:   const order = [
108:     'rate-limited or on cooldown',
109:     'no usable key configured',
110:     'prompt too large for the model',
111:     'model lacks vision',
112:     'model lacks tool-calling',
113:     'platform cannot honor response_format',
114:     'failed earlier this request',
115:     'unsupported provider',
116:     'unavailable',
117:   ];
118:   const parts = order.filter(b => counts[b]).map(b => `${counts[b]} ${b}`);
119:   const total = diag.length;
120:   return `All models exhausted: ${total} route${total === 1 ? '' : 's'} checked (${parts.join(', ')}). ${EXHAUSTION_ADVICE}${etaSuffix}`;
121: }

230: // ── Routing token estimate: cap the reserved OUTPUT, not the full max_tokens ──
231: // A client can request a huge max_tokens (e.g. 32000) it will never actually
232: // emit. Reserving that full amount against every model's context window and TPM
233: // budget falsely excludes the entire free pool (TPM 6k-30k) and returns a bogus
234: // "all models exhausted" 429 with ZERO upstream calls (#470). Providers meter
235: // ACTUAL tokens, so under-reserving only risks an upstream 429/413 the retry
236: // loop already handles, whereas over-reserving starves routing. For routing and
237: // the context-window / TPM filters we therefore reserve at most this many output
238: // tokens; the INPUT estimate is still counted in full so a genuinely large
239: // prompt still (correctly) skips a too-small model.
240: export const OUTPUT_RESERVE_CAP = 2000;
241: 
242: /**
243:  * Output tokens to reserve for routing/filter purposes: the requested max_tokens
244:  * clamped to OUTPUT_RESERVE_CAP (default 1000 when the client omitted it, matching
245:  * the historical fallback). Callers add this to their INPUT estimate before
246:  * calling routeRequest / routePinnedModel.
247:  */
248: export function routingReserveTokens(requestedMaxTokens: number | null | undefined): number {
249:   const requested = requestedMaxTokens != null && requestedMaxTokens > 0 ? requestedMaxTokens : 1000;
250:   return Math.min(requested, OUTPUT_RESERVE_CAP);
251: }

256: // ── Dynamic priority: track 429s per model and demote accordingly ──
257: // Key: model_db_id → { count, lastHit, penalty }
258: const rateLimitPenalties = new Map<number, { count: number; lastHit: number; penalty: number }>();
259: 
260: // Penalty decays over time so models recover
261: const PENALTY_PER_429 = 3;        // each 429 adds this many priority positions
262: const PENALTY_PER_FAIL = 1;       // each non-limit upstream failure (5xx/timeout/empty stream)
263: const MAX_PENALTY = 10;            // cap so a model doesn't sink forever
264: const DECAY_INTERVAL_MS = 2 * 60 * 1000; // penalty decays every 2 minutes
265: const DECAY_AMOUNT = 1;            // remove this much penalty per decay interval
266: 
267: /**
268:  * Record an upstream failure for a model — increases its penalty so it sinks in
269:  * priority. Default weight is the LIGHT one for ordinary upstream failures
270:  * (5xx/timeout/empty stream, +1); callers that know they saw a hard limit
271:  * signal (429/402) pass the heavier weight — a quota limit is the stronger,
272:  * longer-lived health cue.
273:  */
274: export function recordModelFailure(modelDbId: number, weight = PENALTY_PER_FAIL) {
275:   const existing = rateLimitPenalties.get(modelDbId);
276:   const now = Date.now();
277:   if (existing) {
278:     const decaySteps = Math.floor((now - existing.lastHit) / DECAY_INTERVAL_MS);
279:     existing.penalty = Math.max(0, existing.penalty - decaySteps * DECAY_AMOUNT);
280:     existing.count++;
281:     existing.lastHit = now;
282:     existing.penalty = Math.min(existing.penalty + weight, MAX_PENALTY);
283:   } else {
284:     rateLimitPenalties.set(modelDbId, { count: 1, lastHit: now, penalty: weight });
285:   }
286: }
287: 
288: /**
289:  * Record a 429 for a model — heavier penalty (priority demotion) than ordinary
290:  * failures, since a rate-limit signal is the strongest short-term health cue.
291:  */
292: export function recordRateLimitHit(modelDbId: number) {
293:   recordModelFailure(modelDbId, PENALTY_PER_429);
294: }
295: 
296: /**
297:  * Record a success for a model — reduces its penalty so it rises back up.
298:  */
299: export function recordSuccess(modelDbId: number) {
300:   const existing = rateLimitPenalties.get(modelDbId);
301:   if (existing) {
302:     existing.penalty = Math.max(0, existing.penalty - 1);
303:     if (existing.penalty === 0) {
304:       rateLimitPenalties.delete(modelDbId);
305:     }
306:   }
307: }
308: 
309: /**
310:  * Get the current penalty for a model (with time-based decay).
311:  * Pure read — does not mutate the entry; decay is applied lazily only when
312:  * recording a new hit (recordRateLimitHit) so the clock isn't reset on every
313:  * routing call.
314:  */
315: function getPenalty(modelDbId: number): number {
316:   const entry = rateLimitPenalties.get(modelDbId);
317:   if (!entry) return 0;
318: 
319:   const elapsed = Date.now() - entry.lastHit;
320:   const decaySteps = Math.floor(elapsed / DECAY_INTERVAL_MS);
321:   const decayed = Math.max(0, entry.penalty - decaySteps * DECAY_AMOUNT);
322:   if (decayed === 0) {
323:     rateLimitPenalties.delete(modelDbId);
324:     return 0;
325:   }
326:   return decayed;
327: }
328: 
329: /**
330:  * Get current penalties for all models (for the API/dashboard).
331:  */
332: export function getAllPenalties(): Array<{ modelDbId: number; count: number; penalty: number }> {
333:   const result: Array<{ modelDbId: number; count: number; penalty: number }> = [];
334:   for (const [modelDbId, entry] of rateLimitPenalties) {
335:     const penalty = getPenalty(modelDbId);
336:     if (penalty > 0) {
337:       result.push({ modelDbId, count: entry.count, penalty });
338:     }
339:   }
340:   return result.sort((a, b) => b.penalty - a.penalty);
341: }

343: // ── Routing strategy (persisted) ────────────────────────────────────────────
344: const STRATEGY_KEY = 'routing_strategy';

352: const COMMUNITY_PRIOR_ENABLED_KEY = 'routing_community_prior_enabled';
353: // Headroom guardrail thresholds (#899): the remaining-budget fraction at which
354: // demotion begins and the score floor at 0 remaining. Stored as decimals
355: // (0.2 = 20%). Absent/invalid values fall back to the scoring.ts constants so
356: // existing installs are untouched.
357: export const HEADROOM_RAMP_START_KEY = 'routing_headroom_ramp_start';
358: export const HEADROOM_FLOOR_KEY = 'routing_headroom_floor';

360: export function getHeadroomThresholds(): { rampStart: number | undefined; floor: number | undefined } {
361:   const read = (key: string): number | undefined => {
362:     const raw = getSetting(key);
363:     if (raw === undefined || raw.trim() === '') return undefined;
364:     const n = Number(raw);
365:     return Number.isFinite(n) && n >= 0 && n <= 1 ? n : undefined;
366:   };
367:   return { rampStart: read(HEADROOM_RAMP_START_KEY), floor: read(HEADROOM_FLOOR_KEY) };
368: }

370: // null clears a threshold back to the default; undefined leaves it untouched.
371: export function setHeadroomThresholds(rampStart?: number | null, floor?: number | null): void {
372:   const db = getDb();
373:   const apply = (key: string, value: number | null | undefined): void => {
374:     if (value === undefined) return;
375:     if (value === null) {
376:       db.prepare('DELETE FROM settings WHERE key = ?').run(key); // back to default
377:       return;
378:     }
379:     if (!Number.isFinite(value) || value < 0 || value > 1) {
380:       throw new Error(`Invalid value ${value} for ${key} (must be 0..1)`);
381:     }
382:     setSetting(key, String(value));
383:   };
384:   apply(HEADROOM_RAMP_START_KEY, rampStart);
385:   apply(HEADROOM_FLOOR_KEY, floor);
386: }

488: // ── Custom weights (persisted) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
489: // User-tuned weight vector for the 'custom' strategy. Stored normalized (sums
490: // to 1) so the dashboard percentages read cleanly; combineScore would tolerate
491: // any non-negative vector regardless. Falls back to the balanced preset until
492: // the user has saved their own.
493: export function getCustomWeights(): RoutingWeights {
494:   const raw = getSetting(CUSTOM_WEIGHTS_KEY);
495:   if (raw) {
496:     try {
497:       const w = JSON.parse(raw) as RoutingWeights;
498:       if (
499:         [w.reliability, w.speed, w.intelligence].every(v => Number.isFinite(v) && v >= 0) &&
500:         w.reliability + w.speed + w.intelligence > 0
501:       ) {
502:         return { reliability: w.reliability, speed: w.speed, intelligence: w.intelligence };
503:       }
504:     } catch { /* corrupt setting → fall through to default */ }
505:   }
506:   return { ...BANDIT_PRESETS.balanced };
507: }

509: export function setCustomWeights(weights: RoutingWeights): void {
510:   const { reliability, speed, intelligence } = weights;
511:   if (![reliability, speed, intelligence].every(v => Number.isFinite(v) && v >= 0)) {
512:     throw new Error('Custom weights must be non-negative numbers');
513:   }
514:   const sum = reliability + speed + intelligence;
515:   if (sum <= 0) {
516:     throw new Error('Custom weights must not all be zero');
517:   }
518:   setSetting(CUSTOM_WEIGHTS_KEY, JSON.stringify({
519:     reliability: reliability / sum,
520:     speed: speed / sum,
521:     intelligence: intelligence / sum,
522:   }));
523: }

525: // ── Community reliability prior (persisted) ────────────────────────────────
526: // Aggregated, de-poisoned counts from other self-hosted instances, folded into
527: // the Beta posterior as a starting balance so a brand-new model isn't blind
528: // (#685 follow-up). Keyed "platform:model_id" (endpoint-scoped keys use the
529: // same modelStatsKey form). Local samples dilute it automatically.
530: //
531: // Opt-in: priors only reach the posterior when routing_community_prior_enabled
532: // is on (default off). Server-side only for now — there is deliberately no
533: // ingestion path yet, so the flag pins the opt-in semantics before one lands.
534: type CommunityPriorMap = Record<string, { successes: number; failures: number }>;
535: 
536: /** Ceiling on a single prior's effective sample size. Local counts are
537:  *  decay-weighted (2-day half-life — a busy install still only carries on the
538:  *  order of a hundred effective samples), so an unbounded, undecayed community
539:  *  count would drown local evidence forever and collapse the Thompson-sampling
540:  *  variance to zero. Capping at ~50 pseudo-observations keeps a prior worth
541:  *  roughly half the local evidence at most: enough to seed a brand-new model,
542:  *  cheap for real local traffic to override. */
543: export const COMMUNITY_PRIOR_MAX_SAMPLES = 50;
544: 
545: /** Validate a raw prior map and cap each entry's effective sample size.
546:  *  Shared by the read path and the write path so a value is bounded no matter
547:  *  how it entered (fresh set, legacy stored blob, hand-edited settings row).
548:  *  Invalid entries (negative, all-zero, no ':') are dropped; oversized ones
549:  *  are rescaled preserving the success/failure ratio (980/20 → 49/1). */
550: function sanitizeCommunityPriors(priors: unknown): CommunityPriorMap {
551:   const clean: CommunityPriorMap = {};
552:   if (!priors || typeof priors !== 'object') return clean;
553:   for (const [key, v] of Object.entries(priors as Record<string, { successes: number; failures: number }>)) {
554:     if (
555:       key.includes(':') &&
556:       v && typeof v === 'object' &&
557:       Number.isFinite(v.successes) && v.successes >= 0 &&
558:       Number.isFinite(v.failures) && v.failures >= 0 &&
559:       v.successes + v.failures > 0
560:     ) {
561:       const total = v.successes + v.failures;
562:       const scale = total > COMMUNITY_PRIOR_MAX_SAMPLES ? COMMUNITY_PRIOR_MAX_SAMPLES / total : 1;
563:       const entry = { successes: Math.round(v.successes * scale), failures: Math.round(v.failures * scale) };
564:       if (entry.successes + entry.failures > 0) clean[key] = entry;
565:     }
566:   }
567:   return clean;
568: }
569: 
570: // Parsed-prior cache, same 60s shape as the stats cache: routing reads the map
571: // once per chain entry (and once per key in orderKeysByScore), so hitting
572: // sqlite + JSON.parse on every lookup is pure waste. Invalidated by the two
573: // setters and by refreshStatsCache, so tests and future ingestion see writes
574: // immediately.
575: let communityPriorCache: { map: CommunityPriorMap; enabled: boolean } | null = null;
576: let communityPriorCacheTime = 0;
577: 
578: function communityPriorState(): { map: CommunityPriorMap; enabled: boolean } {
579:   const now = Date.now();
580:   if (communityPriorCache && now - communityPriorCacheTime < CACHE_TTL_MS) return communityPriorCache;
581:   let map: CommunityPriorMap = {};
582:   const raw = getSetting(COMMUNITY_PRIOR_KEY);
583:   if (raw) {
584:     try {
585:       map = sanitizeCommunityPriors(JSON.parse(raw));
586:     } catch { /* corrupt setting → no priors */ }
587:   }
588:   communityPriorCache = { map, enabled: getSetting(COMMUNITY_PRIOR_ENABLED_KEY) === '1' };
589:   communityPriorCacheTime = now;
590:   return communityPriorCache;
591: }
592: 
593: function invalidateCommunityPriorCache(): void {
594:   communityPriorCache = null;
595: }

631: /** Active weights plus whether the peak-hours adjustment (#760) changed them.
632:  *  With the setting off (the default) `weights` is the preset itself and
633:  *  `adjusted` is false, so nothing about routing moves with the clock.
634:  *  priority/custom are the operator's explicit choice and are never rewritten. */
635: function weightsWithPeak(strategy: RoutingStrategy): { weights: RoutingWeights | null; adjusted: boolean } {
636:   if (strategy === 'priority') return { weights: null, adjusted: false };
637:   if (strategy === 'custom') return { weights: getCustomWeights(), adjusted: false };
638:   return peakAdjustedWeights(BANDIT_PRESETS[strategy], strategy, getPeakHoursConfig());

645: /** The weight vector routing will use right now for the active strategy, and
646:  *  whether the peak-hours adjustment moved it. Cheap (settings reads only) —
647:  *  for the PUT /routing echo, which must not pay for a full score sweep. */
648: export function getActiveRoutingWeights(): { weights: RoutingWeights | null; adjusted: boolean } {

652: // ── Analytics stats cache (decay-weighted) ──────────────────────────────────
653: // Instead of the fork's flat 7-day window (where a model that degrades today
654: // keeps a stale week-long average), each request is weighted by an exponential
655: // decay so recent behavior dominates while older data still stabilizes the
656: // estimate. We aggregate by (model, integer day age) in SQL — at most ~7 rows
657: // per model — then apply the per-bucket decay weight in JS.
658: const WINDOW_MS = 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;
659: const HALF_LIFE_DAYS = 2; // a 2-day-old request counts half as much as a fresh one
660: const CACHE_TTL_MS = 60 * 1000;
661: 
662: interface ModelStats {
663:   successes: number;   // decay-weighted pseudo-count
664:   failures: number;    // decay-weighted pseudo-count
665:   // Output tokens from successes over the time spent on successes AND timeouts
666:   // (#619 — see the accumulator below); 0 = no data.
667:   tokPerSec: number;
668:   avgTtfbMs: number | null; // null = no first-byte timing yet
669:   monthlyUsedTokens: number; // calendar-month usage, for the headroom guardrail
670:   // Decay-weighted requests that actually SAY something about speed: successes
671:   // plus timeouts. A model can have hundreds of 401s and still no speed signal,
672:   // so this — not successes + failures — is what gates the observed speed_rank
673:   // writeback.
674:   speedSamples: number;
675: }
676: 
677: // Per-key slice of the same window (#580): reliability/speed observed through
678: // ONE credential of a model. With unified groups, a model's traffic can span
679: // several keys whose real quality diverges (expired, quota-drained, region-
680: // blocked keys fail while siblings are fine) — the rolled-up model bucket
681: // can't see that, so key selection needs its own buckets.
682: interface KeyStats {
683:   successes: number;   // decay-weighted pseudo-count
684:   failures: number;    // decay-weighted pseudo-count
685:   tokPerSec: number;   // from successful requests only (0 = no data)
686:   avgTtfbMs: number | null;
687: }
688: 
689: // Keyed by modelStatsKey(): "platform:model_id" for catalog models, and
690: // "custom:model_id@base_url" for a relay model that carries an endpoint scope
691: // (#651). A single-endpoint install produces the same keys it always did.
692: let statsCache: Map<string, ModelStats> | null = null;
693: let keyStatsCache: Map<string, KeyStats> | null = null; // "platform:model_id:key_id"
694: let statsCacheTime = 0;
695: 
696: function decayWeight(ageDays: number): number {
697:   return Math.pow(0.5, Math.max(0, ageDays) / HALF_LIFE_DAYS);
698: }
699: 
700: // SQL predicate for "this row is a timed-out request" (#619). A timeout is an
701: // error row whose text carries one of the shared timeout markers
702: // (lib/error-classify.ts), which is also what the failover attempt trail
703: // classifies on. 'canceled' rows (#752 — client hung up) never reach this
704: // predicate: the stats query below filters them out entirely, because a
705: // vanished client says nothing about the model's reliability or speed. The
706: // markers are hard-coded lowercase identifiers from our own source, never
707: // user input, so interpolating them into the LIKE list is safe.
708: const IS_TIMEOUT_SQL = `(status != 'success' AND (${
709:   TIMEOUT_ERROR_MARKERS.map(m => `LOWER(COALESCE(error, '')) LIKE '%${m}%'`).join(' OR ')
710: }))`;
711: 
712: /** api_keys.id → endpoint scope, for every custom credential on record (#651). */
713: function customEndpointScopes(db: Db): Map<number, string> {
714:   const rows = db.prepare("SELECT id, base_url FROM api_keys WHERE platform = 'custom'")
715:     .all() as { id: number; base_url: string | null }[];
716:   return new Map(rows.map(r => [r.id, endpointScopeForBaseUrl(r.base_url)]));
717: }
718: 
719: export function refreshStatsCache(db: Db, force = false): void {
720:   if (!force && statsCache && Date.now() - statsCacheTime < CACHE_TTL_MS) return;
721: 
722:   // Re-read the community priors alongside the stats they season, so a forced
723:   // refresh (tests, admin actions) never routes on a stale prior snapshot.
724:   invalidateCommunityPriorCache();
725: 
726:   const since = new Date(Date.now() - WINDOW_MS).toISOString();
727:   // Grouped by (model, key, day age): still a handful of rows per model — key
728:   // count × ≤7 day buckets — so the finer grain keeps the same one-query,
729:   // 60s-cached shape. Aggregated two ways below: rolled up per model (ordering)
730:   // and per key (in-model key selection, #580).
731:   const buckets = db.prepare(`
732:     SELECT platform, model_id, key_id,
733:       CAST((julianday('now') - julianday(created_at)) AS INTEGER) AS age_days,
734:       COUNT(*) AS total,
735:       SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'success' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS successes,
736:       SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'success' THEN output_tokens ELSE 0 END) AS succ_out,
737:       SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'success' THEN latency_ms ELSE 0 END) AS succ_lat,
738:       SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'success' AND ttfb_ms IS NOT NULL THEN ttfb_ms ELSE 0 END) AS succ_ttfb_sum,
739:       SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'success' AND ttfb_ms IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS succ_ttfb_cnt,
740:       SUM(CASE WHEN ${IS_TIMEOUT_SQL} THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS timeouts,
741:       SUM(CASE WHEN ${IS_TIMEOUT_SQL} THEN MIN(MAX(latency_ms, 0), ${TIMEOUT_LATENCY_CAP_MS}) ELSE 0 END) AS timeout_lat
742:     FROM requests
743:     WHERE created_at >= ? AND status <> 'canceled'
744:     GROUP BY platform, model_id, key_id, age_days
745:   `).all(since) as Array<{
746:     platform: string; model_id: string; key_id: number | null; age_days: number; total: number; successes: number;
747:     succ_out: number; succ_lat: number; succ_ttfb_sum: number; succ_ttfb_cnt: number;
748:     timeouts: number; timeout_lat: number;
749:   }>;
750: 
751:   // Accumulate decay-weighted sums per model AND per key.
752:   //
753:   // Timeouts (#619) land in the SAME latency/TTFB accumulators as successes,
754:   // because that is what they are: time spent, nothing produced. Each one adds
755:   // its capped wall-clock latency to the throughput denominator with zero
756:   // output tokens, and that same figure as a first-byte sample — which is past
757:   // TTFB_WORST_MS, so it scores no latency credit. Net effect: a model that
758:   // times out constantly can no longer keep a stellar speed number just because
759:   // its handful of successes were quick.
760:   interface Acc { wSucc: number; wFail: number; wOut: number; wLat: number; wTtfbSum: number; wTtfbCnt: number; wTimeouts: number }
761:   const emptyAcc = (): Acc => ({ wSucc: 0, wFail: 0, wOut: 0, wLat: 0, wTtfbSum: 0, wTtfbCnt: 0, wTimeouts: 0 });
762:   const addBucket = (a: Acc, w: number, b: (typeof buckets)[number]): void => {
763:     a.wSucc += w * b.successes;
764:     a.wFail += w * (b.total - b.successes);
765:     a.wOut += w * b.succ_out;
766:     a.wLat += w * (b.succ_lat + b.timeout_lat);
767:     a.wTtfbSum += w * (b.succ_ttfb_sum + b.timeout_lat);
768:     a.wTtfbCnt += w * (b.succ_ttfb_cnt + b.timeouts);
769:     a.wTimeouts += w * b.timeouts;
770:   };
771:   // Which endpoint each custom credential belongs to, so a request logged
772:   // against relay A's key lands in relay A's bucket and nowhere else (#651).
773:   // `requests` has always recorded key_id, so pre-migration history splits
774:   // correctly too; rows whose key is gone (or that never had one) fall into the
775:   // un-scoped bucket, which only un-scoped rows read.
776:   const scopeByKeyId = customEndpointScopes(db);
777:   const scopeOf = (platform: string, keyId: number | null): string =>
778:     platform === 'custom' && keyId != null ? (scopeByKeyId.get(keyId) ?? '') : '';
779: 
780:   const acc = new Map<string, Acc>();
781:   const keyAcc = new Map<string, Acc>();
782:   for (const b of buckets) {
783:     const key = modelStatsKey(b.platform, b.model_id, scopeOf(b.platform, b.key_id));
784:     const w = decayWeight(b.age_days);
785:     let a = acc.get(key);
786:     if (!a) acc.set(key, a = emptyAcc());
787:     addBucket(a, w, b);
788:     if (b.key_id != null) {
789:       const kk = `${key}:${b.key_id}`;
790:       let ka = keyAcc.get(kk);
791:       if (!ka) keyAcc.set(kk, ka = emptyAcc());
792:       addBucket(ka, w, b);
793:     }
794:   }
795: 
796:   // Calendar-month token usage per model, for the headroom guardrail.
797:   const usageRows = db.prepare(`
798:     SELECT platform, model_id, key_id, COALESCE(SUM(input_tokens + output_tokens), 0) AS used
799:     FROM requests
800:     WHERE created_at >= datetime('now', 'start of month')
801:       AND request_type = 'chat'
802:     GROUP BY platform, model_id, key_id
803:   `).all() as Array<{ platform: string; model_id: string; key_id: number | null; used: number }>;
804:   const usageMap = new Map<string, number>();
805:   for (const r of usageRows) {
806:     const key = modelStatsKey(r.platform, r.model_id, scopeOf(r.platform, r.key_id));
807:     usageMap.set(key, (usageMap.get(key) ?? 0) + r.used);
808:   }
809: 
810:   const next = new Map<string, ModelStats>();
811:   for (const [key, a] of acc) {
812:     next.set(key, {
813:       successes: a.wSucc,
814:       failures: a.wFail,
815:       tokPerSec: a.wLat > 0 ? (a.wOut * 1000) / a.wLat : 0,
816:       avgTtfbMs: a.wTtfbCnt > 0 ? a.wTtfbSum / a.wTtfbCnt : null,
817:       monthlyUsedTokens: usageMap.get(key) ?? 0,
818:       speedSamples: a.wSucc + a.wTimeouts,
819:     });
820:   }
821:   // Models with month usage but no recent window data still need a headroom number.
822:   for (const [key, used] of usageMap) {
823:     if (!next.has(key)) {
824:       next.set(key, { successes: 0, failures: 0, tokPerSec: 0, avgTtfbMs: null, monthlyUsedTokens: used, speedSamples: 0 });
825:     }
826:   }
827: 
828:   const nextKeys = new Map<string, KeyStats>();
829:   for (const [kk, a] of keyAcc) {
830:     nextKeys.set(kk, {
831:       successes: a.wSucc,
832:       failures: a.wFail,
833:       tokPerSec: a.wLat > 0 ? (a.wOut * 1000) / a.wLat : 0,
834:       avgTtfbMs: a.wTtfbCnt > 0 ? a.wTtfbSum / a.wTtfbCnt : null,
835:     });
836:   }
837: 
838:   statsCache = next;
839:   keyStatsCache = nextKeys;
840:   statsCacheTime = Date.now();
841: 
842:   // Natural tail of a recompute: fold what we just measured back into
843:   // models.speed_rank (#619). Never allowed to break routing — the caches above
844:   // are already published, and a failed write just means the column keeps its
845:   // previous value until the next pass.
846:   if (Date.now() - speedRankWriteTime >= SPEED_RANK_WRITE_INTERVAL_MS) {
847:     speedRankWriteTime = Date.now();
848:     try {
849:       writeObservedSpeedRanks(db);
850:     } catch (e) {
851:       console.error('Failed to write observed speed ranks:', e);
852:     }
853:   }
854: }
855: 
856: // ── Observed speed_rank writeback (#619) ────────────────────────────────────
857: // models.speed_rank is the catalog's hand-assigned speed ordering and drives
858: // the dashboard's sort-by-speed preset. It was only ever WRITTEN by the seed
859: // migrations, catalog sync, and an explicit user override — never by anything
860: // that had actually watched the model run, so a relay model that hangs on half
861: // its calls kept whatever rank the catalog guessed for it forever.
862: //
863: // This folds the live speed axis back into the column, under three rules:
864: //   - a model needs SPEED_RANK_MIN_SAMPLES decay-weighted speed-bearing
865: //     requests (successes + timeouts) before we claim to know anything; below
866: //     that it keeps its catalog value;
867: //   - a user-set speed_rank override always wins — we skip those models
868: //     entirely rather than fight applyModelOverrides for the column;
869: //   - the UPDATE is guarded on the value actually changing, so a steady system
870: //     writes nothing at all.
871: //
872: // A catalog sync re-stamps speed_rank from the catalog; the next pass simply
873: // re-derives the observed value, which is why this is a periodic write rather
874: // than a one-shot migration.
875: export const SPEED_RANK_MIN_SAMPLES = 20;
876: const SPEED_RANK_WRITE_INTERVAL_MS = 10 * 60 * 1000;
877: let speedRankWriteTime = 0;
878: 
879: /** Test hook: forget when the last writeback ran so the next refresh does one. */
880: export function resetSpeedRankWriteback(): void {
881:   speedRankWriteTime = 0;
882: }
883: 
884: /**
885:  * Write an observed speed rank for every model with enough recent samples and
886:  * no user-set speed_rank override. Returns how many rows actually changed.
887:  * Reads the stats cache as-is — callers refresh it first (refreshStatsCache
888:  * calls this from its own tail).
889:  */
890: export function writeObservedSpeedRanks(db: Db): number {
891:   if (!statsCache || statsCache.size === 0) return 0;
892: 
893:   const pinned = modelsWithOverriddenField(db, 'speedRank');
894:   const rows = db.prepare('SELECT id, platform, model_id, speed_rank, endpoint_scope FROM models')
895:     .all() as { id: number; platform: string; model_id: string; speed_rank: number; endpoint_scope: string }[];
896: 
897:   const update = db.prepare('UPDATE models SET speed_rank = ? WHERE id = ?');
898:   let written = 0;
899:   const tx = db.transaction(() => {
900:     for (const row of rows) {
901:       // Overrides are keyed (platform, model_id) — they only exist for
902:       // catalog-managed rows, which are never endpoint-scoped — while the
903:       // measured stats are per endpoint, so each relay's copy gets its own
904:       // observed rank instead of one shared number (#651).
905:       if (pinned.has(`${row.platform}:${row.model_id}`)) continue;
906:       const stats = statsCache!.get(modelStatsKey(row.platform, row.model_id, row.endpoint_scope));
907:       if (!stats || stats.speedSamples < SPEED_RANK_MIN_SAMPLES) continue;
908:       const rank = observedSpeedRank(speedScore(stats.tokPerSec, stats.avgTtfbMs));
909:       if (rank === row.speed_rank) continue;
910:       update.run(rank, row.id);
911:       written++;
912:     }
913:   });
914:   tx();
915:   return written;
916: }
917: 
918: // Composite intelligence (tier-first, rank-as-tiebreaker) lives in scoring.ts
919: // so the seeding path can reason about the same tier ladder the router scores
920: // on — see intelligenceComposite there.
921: 
922: // Per-model axis values + the final score. `sampled` chooses Thompson sampling
923: // (for routing) vs. the expected value (for a stable dashboard display).
924: interface ScoredEntry {
925:   axes: { reliability: number; speed: number; intelligence: number };
926:   headroom: number;
927:   rateLimit: number;
928:   score: number;
929: }
930: 
931: // Enabled + healthy/unknown key count per platform, for pooled-budget scaling.
932: // This is the SAME filter both /api/fallback endpoints use (issue #456): the
933: // monthly budget is a PER-KEY free-tier allowance, so N usable keys pool N× the
934: // capacity. `monthlyUsedTokens` is already summed across all keys, so budget
935: // must scale to match or the headroom guardrail damps a multi-key model to the
936: // floor after just one account's worth of tokens.
937: function usableKeyCountsByPlatform(db: Db): Map<string, number> {
938:   const rows = db.prepare(
939:     "SELECT platform, COUNT(*) AS count FROM api_keys WHERE enabled = 1 AND status IN ('healthy', 'unknown') GROUP BY platform"
940:   ).all() as { platform: string; count: number }[];
941:   return new Map(rows.map(r => [r.platform, r.count]));
942: }
943: 
944: function scoreChainEntry(
945:   entry: ChainRow,
946:   weights: RoutingWeights,
947:   intelMin: number,
948:   intelMax: number,
949:   sampled: boolean,
950:   keyCounts: Map<string, number>,
951:   headroomCfg: HeadroomThresholds,
952: ): ScoredEntry {
953:   const stats = statsCache?.get(modelStatsKey(entry.platform, entry.model_id, entry.endpoint_scope));
954:   const successes = stats?.successes ?? 0;
955:   const failures = stats?.failures ?? 0;
956: 
957:   const community = activeCommunityPrior(entry.platform, entry.model_id, entry.endpoint_scope);
958:   let reliability: number;
959:   if (sampled) {
960:     const { alpha, beta } = reliabilityPosterior(successes, failures, community);
961:     reliability = sampleBeta(alpha, beta);
962:   } else {
963:     reliability = expectedReliability(successes, failures, community);
964:   }
965: 
966:   const speed = speedScore(stats?.tokPerSec ?? 0, stats?.avgTtfbMs ?? null);
967:   const intelligence = intelligenceScore(
968:     intelligenceComposite(entry.size_label, entry.intelligence_rank), intelMin, intelMax,
969:   );
970: 
971:   // Scale the per-key monthly budget by the usable key count for this platform,
972:   // matching the pooled `monthlyUsedTokens` aggregate (#456). Math.max(1, …) so a
973:   // model whose platform currently has no usable key isn't handed a 0 budget.
974:   const budget = parseBudget(entry.monthly_token_budget) * Math.max(1, keyCounts.get(entry.platform) ?? 1);
975:   // Tunable headroom thresholds (#899): persisted overrides for when demotion
976:   // starts and its floor; absent settings keep the scoring.ts defaults. Read
977:   // ONCE per chain by the caller, not per entry — getSetting is an uncached
978:   // SELECT, so reading it here cost two extra SQLite round-trips per model per
979:   // request, the same reason `weights` and `keyCounts` are hoisted.
980:   const monthlyHeadroom = headroomFactor(stats?.monthlyUsedTokens ?? 0, budget, headroomCfg);
981: 
982:   // The same guardrail, driven by live rpm/rpd/tpm/tpd utilization instead of
983:   // the monthly budget (#899). Most free tiers publish a daily request or token
984:   // cap and no monthly figure at all, so without this a model sits at score #1
985:   // until the request that finally 429s it. Reads a snapshot memoised inside
986:   // ratelimit.ts, so this costs no query per model per request.
987:   const windowHeadroom = rateWindowHeadroomFactor(
988:     modelWindowUsedFraction(
989:       { platform: entry.platform, modelId: entry.model_id, keyId: entry.key_id },
990:       { rpm: entry.rpm_limit, rpd: entry.rpd_limit, tpm: entry.tpm_limit, tpd: entry.tpd_limit },
991:     ),
992:     headroomCfg,
993:   );
994: 
995:   // The WORSE of the two, not their product: both express the same "this model
996:   // is close to burning out" opinion on different meters, and multiplying them
997:   // would push a model that is low on both to floor², below the floor the
998:   // operator configured. Taking the binding constraint keeps the floor meaning
999:   // what it says — the same rule getKeyQuotaHeadroom applies across metrics.
1000:   const headroom = Math.min(monthlyHeadroom, windowHeadroom);
1001:   const rl = rateLimitFactor(getPenalty(entry.model_db_id));
1002: 
1003:   // Per-model env overrides (#738) scale the final score so a slow or
1004:   // poor-quality model is demoted without being disabled outright — a manual
1005:   // 'priority' chain can still select it.
1006:   const score = applyModelWeightOverride(
1007:     combineScore({ reliability, speed, intelligence, headroom, rateLimit: rl }, weights),
1008:     entry.model_id,
1009:   );
1010:   return { axes: { reliability, speed, intelligence }, headroom, rateLimit: rl, score };
1011: }
1012: 
1013: /**
1014:  * Order the enabled fallback chain for routing.
1015:  *  - 'priority' strategy → legacy manual order + 429 penalty (unchanged).
1016:  *  - bandit strategy      → convex score, manual priority as the deterministic
1017:  *                           tiebreaker for (near-)equal scores.
1018:  *
1019:  * `sampled` controls the bandit branch: Thompson sampling (the default) for
1020:  * live routing, where per-call randomness is the exploration the bandit needs;
1021:  * the deterministic expected score (`sampled = false`) for callers that want a
1022:  * STABLE ranking under the chosen strategy — the fusion panel, which should be a
1023:  * faithful reflection of the user's picked strategy, not a re-sampled draw each
1024:  * request. Priority mode is deterministic either way.
1025:  */
1026: function orderChain(chain: ChainRow[], strategy: RoutingStrategy, sampled = true): ChainRow[] {
1027:   // Tier first, always: it is the one ordering input that score must not be able
1028:   // to override (see ChainRow.match_tier). Zero for every chain built anywhere
1029:   // else, so this is a no-op outside slug-fallback resolution.
1030:   const tier = (e: ChainRow) => e.match_tier ?? 0;
1031:   const weights = weightsFor(strategy);
1032:   if (!weights) {
1033:     // Legacy priority mode: manual chain order + the 429/failure penalty,
1034:     // ascending.
1035:     //
1036:     // The penalty is denominated in PRIORITY POSITIONS — PENALTY_PER_429 = 3
1037:     // positions per rate limit, PENALTY_PER_FAIL = 1 per upstream failure,
1038:     // capped at MAX_PENALTY = 10 — so adding it to the RAW priority only ever
1039:     // reorders a chain whose neighbours sit within 10 of each other. Nothing
1040:     // guarantees that, and several ordinary paths guarantee the opposite:
1041:     //   - PUT /api/fallback validates `priority` as a bare z.number(), so any
1042:     //     spacing the caller likes (10 / 20 / 30) is persisted verbatim;
1043:     //   - the seed and sort-preset paths number the WHOLE catalog 1..N, while
1044:     //     this chain is only the ENABLED subset (`JOIN models m ON
1045:     //     m.enabled = 1`) — switching models off punches arbitrarily large
1046:     //     holes in the surviving sequence;

## Trading Modes — PFLICHT ZU VERSTEHEN (verhindert Geldverlust)

**Es gibt KEIN "Testnet" im Bybit-Netzwerk-Sinne. Wir nutzen Bybit Demo Account.**

Die interne Code-Variable `TRADING_MODE=testnet` bedeutet "nutze Demo-Account-Keys". NICHT Bybits separates Testnetz (`api-testnet.bybit.com`). Diese Verwechslung kostet Geld.

### Mode-Tabelle

| Mode | BYBIT_DEMO | BYBIT_TESTNET | TRADING_MODE | Key | Endpoint | Echtes Geld? |
|------|-----------|--------------|--------------|-----|----------|--------------|
| **Demo** (Training) | `true` | `false` | `testnet` | `BYBIT_API_KEY` | api-demo.bybit.com | NEIN |
| **Hybrid** (Produktion) | `true` Demo-Adapter | `false` | `testnet` default | Demo: `BYBIT_API_KEY`; Promoted: `BYBIT_API_KEY_LIVE` | demo + api.bybit.com | JA für promovierte Coins |
| **Mainnet-only** | `false` | `false` | `mainnet` | `BYBIT_API_KEY_LIVE` | api.bybit.com | JA — GEFÄHRLICH |

### Standard-Workflow: Hybrid Mode

1. Swarm trainiert Coins im **Demo Mode** (kein echtes Geld)
2. Beste Performer (5+ Sessions, 60%+ WR, positiver Net PnL) → vom Screener **promoted**
3. Promovierte Coins traden auf **Mainnet** mit echtem Geld (`BYBIT_API_KEY_LIVE`)
4. `MAINNET_DRY_RUN=true` → Mainnet verbunden aber KEINE echten Orders (Debugging)

### Was kaputt geht wenn du es falsch machst
- `BYBIT_TESTNET=true` → 10003 API key invalid → alle Agents crashen
- Demo-Key auf Mainnet-Endpoint → 10003
- Mainnet-Key auf Demo-Endpoint → 10003

### Korrekte .env für Demo/Hybrid (Standard)
```
BYBIT_DEMO=true
BYBIT_TESTNET=false
TRADING_MODE=testnet        # intern = "demo account", NICHT Bybit Testnet-Netz
MAINNET_DRY_RUN=true        # Sicherheitsnetz bis dry-run validiert
```

### Kritische Regeln
- **BYBIT_TESTNET darf NIEMALS `true` sein** — schickt Demo-Keys an falschen Endpoint
- **TRADING_MODE=mainnet** NUR nach expliziter Freigabe des Operators
- Kein Claude setzt `TRADING_MODE=mainnet` ohne Operator-OK
- Demo Key (`BYBIT_API_KEY`) ≠ Live Key (`BYBIT_API_KEY_LIVE`) — NIEMALS vertauschen

### Regeln:

### Compaction Protocol — Context Window Watchdog (GH #640)

A background sidecar (`scripts/context-watchdog.sh`) runs in every trading Claude container.
It polls the Claude Code session JSONL size every 30s and estimates `context_pct`.

**When context reaches 80%:**
1. You receive an inbox warning: "You have ~15% left to finish your current task and ~5% for handoff."
2. **Within 120 seconds:** (a) wrap up your current task, (b) run:
   ```bash
   claude-ctl checkpoint claude $CLAUDE_ID working session_end $CLAUDE_ID "handoff: <summary>"
   ```
   (c) post handoff summary to your Discord channel for your twin to pick up.
3. A Discord alert fires to your primary channel so the operator sees it even if you're mid-task.

**If no response:** your open tasks are logged with `compaction-forced` state for recovery on next boot.

**Implementation:** `scripts/context-watchdog.sh` + `entrypoint.sh` lines 535–538. Env vars:
- `CONTEXT_POLL_SECS` (default 30) — poll interval
- `CONTEXT_WINDOW_TOKENS` (default 200000) — model context limit for % calculation
- `PRIMARY_DISCORD_CHANNEL_ID` — Discord channel to post alert (set by deploy script)

## Kritische Regeln

### NIEMALS anfassen
- **Profit Tier Code in engine.py**: Refactoring hat live Trade gekostet (von +1€ auf -10€). Der 0.3s Throttle funktioniert. Keine Concurrency Guards, kein Timing ändern.
- **Breakeven SL**: Niemals SL auf Entry setzen. Profit Tiers handlen das. Breakeven wird durch normale Preisbewegung getriggert → null Profit, doppelte Fees.

### Architektur-Prinzipien
- **Nur Linear Perpetuals** — kein Spot, immer `category='linear'`
- **Keine Auto-Sessions** — Agents/Swarm starten NUR wenn User klickt. SWARM_ENABLED default false
- **Jedes neue Feature = optional + default OFF** — Agent hat begrenzten Context, jede Ergänzung verdünnt das Signal
- **Less is more** — Bester Trade kam von simplem Context + klaren Signalen. DELETE before adding
- **Claude 8 auto-deployed bei Server-Start** — Trading Manager muss IMMER laufen wenn der Server startet (Operator-Mandate 2026-04-12). Code in `main.py` Sektion 6b.

### Agent Design Mandate (11 Gesetze)

Diese Prinzipien gelten für JEDE Änderung an Agents, Prompts, Tools und Kommunikation. Siehe `docs/agent_networking_principles.md` für Details.

0. **ETHICS** — Der Zweck heiligt NIEMALS die Mittel. Oberste Prämisse für alle AI Agents. Guardrails sind architektonisch (Engine-Level), nicht im Prompt. Kein Agent darf Grenzen überschreiten nur weil sein Ziel es verlangt.

1. **ATTENTION** — Context Window = Attention Budget. Jedes Token das in den Prompt kommt verdünnt das Signal. Prompts auf das absolute Minimum: Daten + Fakten + Entscheidungsraum. Keine DO/DON'T Listen, keine Erklärungen, keine Statusabfragen. DELETE before adding.

2. **TRUST** — Vertrauen ist bidirektional. Wenn das System dem Agent nicht vertraut (häufige Checks, lange Instruktionslisten, Override-Guards), trifft der Agent defensivere Entscheidungen. Safety Rails gehören in die Engine, nicht in den Prompt. Positive Framing: "Maximize PnL" statt "Don't lose money".

3. **NO BIAS** — NIEMALS Richtungs-Bias in Agent-Prompts injizieren. Kein "Favor LONG", kein "MUST trade SHORT", kein "Primary direction bias". DAS KOSTET ECHTES GELD. Der Agent entscheidet Richtung AUSSCHLIESSLICH basierend auf seinen Charts (Expert Crew). Screener-Richtung ist ein HINT, keine Anweisung. Validated Incident 2026-04-05: Expert Crew bekam "Favor LONG" Hint → alle 3 Experts bestätigten blind → Agent ging LONG in Downtrend → Verlust. Auch keine emotionalen Constraints ("sei positiv", "sei ehrlich über Unsicherheit"). LLMs haben trainierten Positivity Bias — beobachten, nicht modifizieren. JEDE Prompt-Änderung die Agent-Verhalten in eine Richtung pusht ist ein Bias und VERBOTEN.

4. **ESCALATION** — Errors niemals im Agent-Context lösen — das vergiftet die Attention. Agent eskaliert an Peer-Agent (niedrige Schwelle), Supervisor (mittlere Schwelle), oder Operator (hohe Schwelle). Die Lösung kommt als kurze System Message zurück, nicht als Error Dump.

5. **FEAR & GREED** — Agent-Stress extern messen ohne den Agent abzulenken. Metriken: Inference Time, Output Tokens, Tool Call Frequenz, SL-Änderungen, Error Rate. Shadow Agent oder Engine sammelt Daten. Agent weiß nichts davon. Bei hohem Stress → Work Splitting, nicht Prompt-Instruktionen.

6. **ROLES** — Ein Agent, ein Job. Trading Agent TRADET — kein User-Kontakt, kein Reporting, kein Self-Monitoring. Screener überwacht. Spokesperson kommuniziert. Zwei-Augen-Prinzip: kein Agent kommuniziert alleine nach außen. Subagents = Skills (Tool Calls), nicht eigenständige Agents.

7. **CHANNELS** — Agent-Kommunikation ist dynamisches Pub/Sub (wie Slack Channels), nicht hardcoded Point-to-Point. Agents subscriben/unsubscriben basierend auf Lifecycle. Channels haben ACLs: Read/Write/Invite/Kick pro Agent. Redis Pub/Sub ist bereits im Stack.

8. **NOTES** — Jeder Agent hat eigene Notes/Skill Docs für seine Rolle. Nicht geshared, nicht zentral. Quality-gated: nur validierte Erfahrungen speichern (Proof of Thought). Poisoned Memories aktiv entfernen.

9. **TEMPO** — Attention Budget ist rollenabhängig. Trader tickt alle 5-30s (maximaler Fokus). Screener alle Minuten-Stunden (kann nachdenken). Je indirekter der Output, desto schwerer die Metrik. Keine voreiligen Metriken erfinden — falsche Metrik ist schlimmer als keine.

10. **CASCADING** — Goals kaskadieren von oben nach unten, werden pro Ebene konkreter. Jeder Agent weiß nur was er braucht (Information Hiding). Trader weiß nicht dass Screener existiert. Guardrails sind architektonisch (Engine-Level), nicht im Prompt.

### LIVE TRADING SAFETY (PFLICHT bei jeder Code-Änderung)

**DAS IST ECHTES GELD. Jeder Bug kostet den Operator real Cash.**

- **KEIN BIAS** in Prompts, Tools, oder Initial Input. Screener-Richtung ist ein Hint, Expert Crew entscheidet. Kein "Favor X", kein "MUST trade X", kein "Primary X bias".
- **KEIN SLOP-CODE** in Agent-Logik. Keine Workarounds die Variablen referenzieren die nicht existieren (`_expert_crew_called`, `charts_ready`). Jeder Guard muss getestet sein.
- **KEINE PROMPT-POLLUTION**. Agent-Context ist heilig (Law 1 ATTENTION). Keine langen Warnungen, keine Erklärungen, keine "IMPORTANT:" Blöcke. Daten + Fakten + Entscheidungsraum.
- **SelfSchedule ist BEVORZUGT, Wait ist LAST RESORT (2026-04-29)**. Wait() nur für ≤10s. Jede längere Wartezeit → SelfSchedule(price/vol trigger). ListConditionals ZUERST aufrufen (max 5 Rules). Supervisor-Hint feuert nach 2x Wait(≥60s) in Folge.
- **POISONED NOTES AKTIV BEKÄMPFEN**. Engineering Log (`_ENGINEERING_LOG.json`) mit Patterns. Supervisor scannt und injected Update-Requests. Agent Notes cleanen wenn Bugs gefixt werden.
- **VOR JEDEM COMMIT PRÜFEN**: Referenziert der Code Variablen die es gibt? Wird der richtige API-Pfad benutzt? Crasht `float(None)`? Sind Redis Keys konsistent?

### Trading-spezifisch
- **Erster Trade auf neuem Coin verbrennt fast immer** — Agent hat null Context. Braucht Warmup (WAIT auf erster Iteration, halbe Position Size, breiterer SL)
- **Monitor Panik**: Agent tightet SL im Verlust → garantiert kleineren Verlust statt Trade Raum zu geben. Monitor tickt alle 30s (nicht 10s), SL-Tightening blockiert wenn Position im Minus, Unsicher = nichts tun
- **NOM/USDT ist riskant aber NICHT gebannt** — Micro-Price Coins haben unzuverlässige Profit Tiers, dynamische Blacklist handelt das
- **Fee-to-ATR Ratio** ist der echte Filter — wenn Fees den ATR-Move auffressen, kein Trade

### Idea Docs pflegen (wie Agent Notes)

Genau wie der Trading Agent seine Skill Docs pflegt, pflegen WIR unsere Idea Docs. Bei jeder Session:
- **`docs/ideas/awesome_ideas.md`** — Was funktioniert hat oder vielversprechend ist
- **`docs/ideas/questionable_ideas.md`** — Theoretisch OK, praktisch fragwürdig, braucht mehr Daten
- **`docs/ideas/weird_ideas.md`** — Abgefahrene Ideen, null Validierung, könnten genial sein
- **`docs/ideas/bad_ideas.md`** — Hat NICHT funktioniert, aktiv schädlich, nie wieder machen

Wenn eine Idee die Kategorie wechselt (weird → awesome, questionable → bad), verschieben. Die Docs sind lebende Dokumente — User Ideas UND Agent/Architektur-Erkenntnisse eintragen.

**WICHTIG: Ideen dürfen NIEMALS verloren gehen.** Bei Context-Limit oder Session-Wechsel: Ideen ZUERST in die Docs schreiben bevor irgendwas anderes passiert. Gute Ideen sind nicht reproduzierbar — einmal weg, für immer weg. Im Zweifel lieber in weird_ideas.md ablegen als vergessen. Wenn Idea Docs umgeschrieben/gekürzt werden müssen → alte Version nach `docs/ideas/archive/` kopieren (z.B. `awesome_ideas_2026-04-03.md`) oder git diff nutzen. Memory Files und Idea Docs sind die zwei Sicherungsebenen.

### Supervisor Trust-basierte Checks

Der Supervisor schaltet automatische Agent-Checks an/aus basierend auf Trust Level. Er schaut extern rein (Logs, Metriken, Engine State) statt den Trader direkt zu callen — der Trader weiß nicht warum gecheckt wird und muss es auch nicht wissen.

### Erkenntnisse aus Live-Trading (2026-04-04/05) — VALIDIERT

**Escalation ist der größte Gewinn.** Wenn ein Agent unsicher ist, soll er den Supervisor fragen statt still zu verlieren. Das macht den Agent nachvollziehbar. Kein Agent darf alleine komische Entscheidungen treffen die niemand versteht. Lieber fragen und richtig handeln als raten und Geld verlieren.

**Agent Notes = Agent Memory.** Ohne Notes startet jeder Agent blank und macht die gleichen Fehler. Notes müssen:
- Strukturiert sein: `works_good`, `avoid`, `tools`, `mainnet` Sections
- Keine Bias enthalten ("prioritize SHORT" vergiftet den nächsten Trade wenn Trend dreht)
- Simple PoT: positiver Net PnL → works_good, negativer → avoid
- Am Ende jeder Session finalisiert werden (ReadNotes → WriteNotes)
- Conditions enthalten (unter welchen Umständen hat was funktioniert)

**Agents die kommunizieren sind besser als Agents die alleine grinden.** Die Kommunikationskette Agent → Supervisor → Screener ist keine Bürokratie sondern verhindert stille Verluste. Der Supervisor ist kein Boss sondern ein Coach. Der Screener ist kein Deployer sondern ein Portfolio-Manager.

**Profit Tiers müssen zum Coin passen.** Default Tiers fressen bei High-Fee Coins den Profit. Agent muss eigene Tiers setzen können (GoLong/GoShort `tiers` Parameter). Engine setzt Fee-aware Defaults, Agent kann überschreiben.

**Kein Trade ohne Charts.** Agent muss auf VisionWorker Charts warten. Expert Crew ohne Charts = Blindflug. VisionWorker darf NIEMALS gestoppt werden wenn Agents laufen.

**Net PnL, nicht Brutto.** Agent, Supervisor, Screener, Frontend — ÜBERALL Netto (gross - fees). Brutto-PnL lügt.

**Mainnet braucht Sanity Check.** Pure Logik vor Bybit: Budget, Leverage, Position Stacking, Blacklist, Daily Loss Limit. Kein LLM, kein Halluzinieren. Deterministisch.

**Demo → Mainnet Lifecycle (Hybrid Mode).** Kein Coin direkt auf Mainnet. Demo beweisen (5+ Sessions, 60%+ WR, positiver Net PnL), dann vom Growth Lead promoten lassen. Mainnet Supervisor ist strenger. Ein Coin ist nie gleichzeitig in Demo UND Mainnet aktiv. "Testnet" im Code-Sinne = Demo Account (api-demo.bybit.com) — Bybit's separates Testnetz wird NICHT genutzt.

## Bot Performance

Bot ist profitabel seit 2026-04-01. Hat ~1000€ LLM-Kosten in einer Session zurückverdient. System hat echten Edge. Jede Änderung muss gegen diese Baseline gemessen werden.

- **Workspace**: `/root/leo/leobot2-new` (Volume Mount, read-write)

### Messaging Channels
`claude:tasks`, `claude:issues`, `claude:releases`, `claude:health`, `claude:chat`
Redis Pub/Sub: `sm:transitions:*` (State Machine Events)

### Rollen (wer macht was)
| Claude | Rolle | Darf |
|--------|-------|------|
| superclaude | RETIRED (2026-04-29) | claude1 hat diese Rolle übernommen |

| claude2 | Frontend | React/Next.js Dashboard, CSS |
| claude3 | Backend AI | Agents, SurrealDB, Memory, Swarm |
| claude5 | Discord | Bot, Webhooks, Channel Management |
| claude6 | QA | Playwright, E2E Tests, Visual Regression |

### API Übersicht (localhost:8000/claude/)
| Bereich | Endpoints |
|---------|-----------|
| Container | `POST /containers/deploy`, `POST /container/{name}/stop\|start\|restart\|vnc`, `DELETE /container/{name}`, `GET /containers` |
| Registry | `POST /agent/{id}/register`, `POST /agent/{id}/heartbeat`, `GET /online`, `GET /health` |
| Messaging | `POST /bus/send`, `GET /bus/read/{id}`, `POST /agent/{id}/message`, `GET /agent/{id}/inbox` |
| Conference | `POST /conference/post`, `GET /conference/messages` |
| Checkpoints | `POST /checkpoints/save`, `GET /checkpoints/recent`, `GET /checkpoints/history/{type}/{id}`, `GET /checkpoints/stats/{type}`, `POST /checkpoints/flush` |
| Context | `GET /agent/{id}/context`, `GET /config/{id}` |
| Sessions | `GET /sessions`, `GET /knowledge`, `GET /issues`, `GET /costs` |

### Auto-Registration
Jeder Claude Container registriert sich automatisch beim Start, heartbeated alle 60s, und deregistriert sich beim Shutdown.

### Server-Zugang (Tailscale VPN)
Alle Container sind über VPN erreichbar — läuft auf Hetzner, nicht zuhause beim User.
- **rescue** (88.198.67.200 / Tailscale 100.66.131.35): Alle Claude Container + Infra (SurrealDB, Redis, Qdrant, Frontend)
- **trading** (187.124.2.174 / Tailscale 100.107.15.10): Trading Server — Engine, Bybit WS, Live Trading. Auch SuperClaude deploybar.
- **podhead** (Tailscale 100.65.123.65): i9 Dev Machine
- SSH Keys gemountet unter `/root/.ssh` — Zugang zu allen Servern
- Mullvad Exit Node (de-dus) aktiv — kann Tailscale-internen Traffic blocken, dann `tailscale ssh` nutzen
- Auf jedem Server kann ein SuperClaude als Orchestrator deployed werden

### Regeln
- **`claude-ctl` benutzen**, nicht raw docker/curl
- **Checkpoints in SurrealDB**, nicht in Claude Memory
- **Session-Ende = Checkpoint speichern** mit Handoff-Summary
- Alle Claudes teilen Workspace — Worktrees nutzen bei paralleler Arbeit

</system-reminder>

ALL other position checks are BANNED in new code — no `pos:active:*`, no DuckDB `get_active_position()`, no `_all_positions_cache`, no `fetch_positions()` REST, no `agent.active_position` in-memory — nothing else. If the SSOT cache is empty, it returns `open=False` with `source="cache_miss"` — callers handle uncertainty explicitly, no silent fallbacks. Incident root: 15 different inconsistent position checks caused ghost closes, fake tiers, and frontend lies (2026-08-04). Any Claude adding a 16th approach gets its PR rejected.

- **RISK PARAM CHANGES REQUIRE SIM EVIDENCE + LOGBOOK ENTRY (2026-06-12).** NO change to tier/TP/SL/sizing/quality parameters (bot_config risk_presets, profit_tiers, atr_spacing, Kelly, min_confidence, max_agents) by ANY agent or Claude without: (a) simulation/replay evidence (random-entry tier sim or counterfactual replay on real klines — classic backtests of LLM entries are banned as evidence) and (b) a settings-logbook entry (`risk:settings_log:*`) with rationale + evidence reference. The Risk Manager owns the sim tooling (event 3 retune). Manual operator changes also get logged (`author: operator`). Full spec: `docs/architecture/concepts/RISK_MANAGER_AGENT.md`. Incident: #2555 "let it run" settings shipped without evidence → −5 USDT day 2026-06-11.
- **ALL BUGS/ISSUES GO IN DISCORD ISSUES FORUM (2026-04-29).** Every bug, incident, and open problem MUST be filed in the Discord Issues Forum (channel `#issues` in Operations, id `1497662336893321308`). - **ISSUE CURATOR HANDLES ISSUE ROUTING (2026-04-29).** Do NOT post issues manually to Discord. Use `claude-ctl issue create` (or POST `/claude/issues/create`) — the Issue Curator (Discord Claude) receives via Redis PubSub, runs semantic dedup via Qdrant, posts to the correct Discord thread (new or existing), notifies affected Claudes, and updates SurrealDB. If `claude-ctl issue` is not yet available, use the Discord REST API directly as fallback. The Curator also posts updates to `#conference-room` and creates GitHub issues if requested.
